117b1098396ca8510285033a11431056a443f324.title: Observable factorization identities
117b1098396ca8510285033a11431056a443f324.body:
Let \(\mathcal M\) be a latent-shift SCM on finite state spaces \(\mathcal E,\mathcal U,\mathcal W,\mathcal X,\mathcal Y\), and suppose that \(\mathcal M\in\mathfrak M_{+}\) in the sense of \(\cref{obj:def:positive-latent-shift-class}\). Then, for every \(x\in\mathcal X\) and \(y\in\mathcal Y\),
\[
B_x = M R_x,\qquad
b = Mq,\qquad
c_{x,y}=g_{x,y}^{\top}R_x,\qquad
\theta_{x,y}=g_{x,y}^{\top}q .
\]
Moreover, for every \(\lambda\in\Lambda_x(\mathcal D)\), where \(\Lambda_x(\mathcal D)\) is the balancing fiber in \(\cref{obj:def:balancing-fiber}\), the unconditional weight \(\kappa\) induced by \(\lambda\) as in \(\cref{obj:def:unconditional-weight-map}\) satisfies
\[
H_x\kappa=b
\qquad\text{and}\qquad
z_{x,y}^{\top}\kappa=\theta_{x,y}.
\]
Finally, there exists a vector \(h:\mathcal W\to\mathbb R\) such that
\[
H_x^{\top}h=z_{x,y}.
\]

3fe6a8fd6cfa2777c7b4bad375af9b1f7ca0a480.title: Strict rank extension
3fe6a8fd6cfa2777c7b4bad375af9b1f7ca0a480.body:
For any normalized finite latent-shift SCM \(\mathcal M\) on finite state spaces \(\mathcal E,\mathcal U,\mathcal W,\mathcal X,\mathcal Y\), with \(\mathcal M\in\mathfrak M_{+}\) as in \(\cref{obj:def:positive-latent-shift-class}\), the following implication holds for every treatment \(x\in\mathcal X\): if
\[
\operatorname{rank}(B_x)=|\mathcal U|,
\]
then
\[
\{v\in\mathbb R^{\mathcal W}:\exists \lambda\in\mathbb R^{\mathcal E}\text{ with }B_x\lambda=v\}
=
\{v\in\mathbb R^{\mathcal W}:\exists q\in\mathbb R^{\mathcal U}\text{ with }Mq=v\}
\]
and the balancing fiber \(\Lambda_x(\mathcal D)=\{\lambda\in\mathbb R^{\mathcal E}:B_x\lambda=b\}\) from \(\cref{obj:def:balancing-fiber}\) is nonempty.

Moreover, the explicit construction \(\mathcal M^{\star}\) in \(\cref{obj:def:rank-deficient-success-witness}\) satisfies all of the following:
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Positive class.)} \(\mathcal M^{\star}\in\mathfrak M_{+}\).
\item \textbf{(Treatment-wise rank.)} For every \(x\in\operatorname{Fin}(2)\), \(\operatorname{rank}(B_x)=2\).
\item \textbf{(Treatment-wise target span.)} For every \(x\in\operatorname{Fin}(2)\), \(\Lambda_x(\mathcal D)=\{\lambda\in\mathbb R^{\operatorname{Fin}(2)}:B_x\lambda=b\}\) is nonempty.
\item \textbf{(Strict latent cardinality.)} \(2<|\operatorname{Fin}(3)|\).
\end{itemize}

3eedd4e6668ddfb55b31f0036d88cdd1c9dea482.title: Positive full-law converse
3eedd4e6668ddfb55b31f0036d88cdd1c9dea482.body:
Let \(P_O\) be an observed source law and let \(b\) be a target proxy law. Suppose that:
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Compatible fiber.)} The compatible fiber \(\mathfrak F(\mathcal D)\) in \(\cref{obj:def:compatible-fiber}\), with \(\mathcal D=(P_O,b)\), is nonempty, and \(\mathcal M\in\mathfrak F(\mathcal D)\).
\item \textbf{(Factorization and invariance.)} The model \(\mathcal M\) satisfies the source-law factorization in \(\cref{obj:ass:latent-shift-factorization}\) and the target mechanism invariance condition in \(\cref{obj:ass:target-mechanism-invariance}\).
\item \textbf{(Positivity and proxy rank.)} The model \(\mathcal M\) satisfies strict primitive positivity as in \(\cref{obj:ass:strict-primitive-positivity}\), and its proxy channel has full column rank as in \(\cref{obj:ass:proxy-channel-injectivity}\).
\item \textbf{(Target-span failure.)} For the source conditional proxy matrix \(B_x=P_O(W\mid E,x)\),
\[
B_x\lambda \ne b
\]
for every \(\lambda\in\mathbb R^{\mathcal E}\).
\item \textbf{(Separator and offset cell.)} Fix \(y^\circ\in\mathcal Y\) with \(y^\circ\ne y\), fix \(w_{\star}\in\mathcal W\), and let \(h\in\mathcal H_x(\mathcal D)\), where \(\mathcal H_x(\mathcal D)\) is the failure-separator set in \(\cref{obj:def:failure-separator}\).
\end{itemize}
Then there exists \(\varepsilon>0\) such that, for every \(t\in\mathbb R\) with \(|t|<\varepsilon\), the outcome-null perturbation \(f^{(t)}\) from \(\cref{obj:def:outcome-null-perturbation}\), applied at \((x,y,w_{\star})\) and offset at \(y^\circ\), is nonnegative and sums to one over \(y'\) for every \((x',u,w)\). Let \(\mathcal M_t\) be the latent-shift SCM obtained from \(\mathcal M\) by replacing \(f\) with this \(f^{(t)}\) and recomputing \(P_{\mathcal M_t}\) and \(Q_{\mathcal M_t}\). Then
\[
\mathcal M_t\in\mathfrak F(\mathcal D)
\]
and
\[
\theta_{x,y}(\mathcal M_t)-\theta_{x,y}(\mathcal M)
=
t\,h^\top b .
\]
Consequently, the compatible values of \(\theta_{x,y}\) contain the open interval
\[
\bigl(\theta_{x,y}(\mathcal M)-\varepsilon |h^\top b|,
      \theta_{x,y}(\mathcal M)+\varepsilon |h^\top b|\bigr)
\]
inside the identified interval
\[
\Bigl\{\theta_{x,y}(\widetilde{\mathcal M}):
\widetilde{\mathcal M}\in\mathfrak F(\mathcal D)\Bigr\}.
\]

b23143bafeddde53c7aa985366806615afff09dc.title: Target span characterization
b23143bafeddde53c7aa985366806615afff09dc.body:
Let \(\mathcal D=(P_O,b)\) be supplied observed and target-proxy data, let \(x\in\mathcal X\) and \(y\in\mathcal Y\), and let \(\mathcal M_0\) be a latent-shift SCM.  Suppose that:
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Compatible fiber.)} The compatible fiber \(\mathfrak F(\mathcal D)\) of \(\cref{obj:def:compatible-fiber}\) is nonempty.
\item \textbf{(Reference model.)} The reference model satisfies \(\mathcal M_0\in\mathfrak F(\mathcal D)\).
\item \textbf{(Proxy injectivity.)} The reference model \(\mathcal M_0\) satisfies the proxy-channel injectivity condition in \(\cref{obj:ass:proxy-channel-injectivity}\).
\end{itemize}
Write
\[
B_x(w,e)=\frac{\sum_{y'\in\mathcal Y}P_O(e,w,x,y')}
{\sum_{w'\in\mathcal W}\sum_{y'\in\mathcal Y}P_O(e,w',x,y')}
\]
for the conditional proxy matrix of \(\mathcal M_0\) at treatment \(x\), and, for each \(\mathcal M\in\mathfrak F(\mathcal D)\), write
\[
c_{x,y}^{\mathcal M}(e)=
\frac{\sum_{w\in\mathcal W}P_O(e,w,x,y)}
{\sum_{w\in\mathcal W}\sum_{y'\in\mathcal Y}P_O(e,w,x,y')}
\]
for its conditional outcome vector at \((x,y)\).  Then the identified interval for the target interventional probability
\[
\theta_{x,y}(\mathcal M)=\sum_{u\in\mathcal U}\sum_{w\in\mathcal W}q_{\mathcal M}(u)M_{\mathcal M}(w,u)f_{\mathcal M,x,y}(u,w)
\]
over \(\mathfrak F(\mathcal D)\) is a singleton if and only if the balancing fiber \(\Lambda_x(\mathcal D)=\{\lambda:B_x\lambda=b\}\) of \(\cref{obj:def:balancing-fiber}\) is nonempty.  Moreover, every \(\lambda\in\Lambda_x(\mathcal D)\) satisfies, for every \(\mathcal M\in\mathfrak F(\mathcal D)\),
\[
\theta_{x,y}(\mathcal M)=\sum_{e\in\mathcal E}c_{x,y}^{\mathcal M}(e)\lambda(e).
\]
In particular, for all \(\lambda,\lambda'\in\Lambda_x(\mathcal D)\),
\[
\sum_{e\in\mathcal E}c_{x,y}^{\mathcal M_0}(e)\lambda(e)
=
\sum_{e\in\mathcal E}c_{x,y}^{\mathcal M_0}(e)\lambda'(e).
\]

f384bc76added881a27a23257f9e619e9814a874.title: Finite-sample projection coverage
f384bc76added881a27a23257f9e619e9814a874.body:
Let \(\mathcal M\) be a latent-shift SCM on finite state spaces \(\mathcal E,\mathcal U,\mathcal W,\mathcal X,\mathcal Y\), let \(P_O\) be an observed source law, and let \(b\) be a target proxy law. Fix \(x\in\mathcal X\) and \(y\in\mathcal Y\). Suppose that
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Positive latent shift.)} \(\mathcal M\in\mathfrak M_{+}\) in the sense of \(\cref{obj:def:positive-latent-shift-class}\).
\item \textbf{(Compatibility.)} \(\mathcal M\in\mathfrak F(\mathcal D)\), with \(\mathcal D=(P_O,b)\), in the sense of \(\cref{obj:def:compatible-fiber}\).
\item \textbf{(Balancing feasibility.)} The affine balancing set \(\Lambda_x(\mathcal D)\) from \(\cref{obj:def:balancing-fiber}\) is nonempty; equivalently, there exists \(\lambda:\mathcal E\to\mathbb R\) such that \(B_x\lambda=b\).
\item \textbf{(Sample sizes and level.)} The sample sizes satisfy \(n_s>0\) and \(n_t>0\), and the nominal error level satisfies \(0<\alpha<1\).
\end{itemize}
Then, under the two-sample product law \(\mathbb P_{\mathcal M}^{\,n_s,n_t}\) for the independent source observations and target proxy draws,
\[
1-\alpha
\le
\mathbb P_{\mathcal M}^{\,n_s,n_t}
\left\{
\theta_{x,y}\in
\widehat C_{x,y,1-\alpha}
\right\},
\]
where \(\theta_{x,y}=\sum_{u\in\mathcal U}\sum_{w\in\mathcal W}q(u)M(w,u)f_{x,y}(u,w)\), and \(\widehat C_{x,y,1-\alpha}\) is the concentration-calibrated projection set of \(\cref{obj:def:concentration-projection-set}\) formed from \(\widehat H_x\), \(\widehat z_{x,y}\), \(\widehat b\), \(n_s\), \(n_t\), and \(\alpha\).

9e03de31105cdd1192e65e55726937bb096bc027.title: Uniform coverage forces Wald separation
9e03de31105cdd1192e65e55726937bb096bc027.body:
Fix a source allocation limit \(p\in(0,1)\), an error level \(\alpha\in(0,1)\), and deterministic allocation sequences \(n_s(n)\) and \(n_t(n)\) satisfying \(\cref{ass:triangular-allocation}\). For each \(n\), write \(\Omega_n=\Omega(n_s(n),n_t(n))\). Then there exist a fixed latent-shift SCM \(\mathcal M^{(0)}\) with binary \(\mathcal E,\mathcal U,\mathcal W,\mathcal Y\) and singleton \(\mathcal X\), and a two-sample triangular array \(\mathbb M^{(1)}=(\mathcal M^{(1)}_n)_{n\ge 0}\) on the same state spaces and allocation sequences, such that:
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Regular baseline.)} \(\mathcal M^{(0)}\in\mathcal R_{1,1/4,1/16}\) for the treatment \(x=0\), outcome \(y=1\), and source allocation limit \(p\).
\item \textbf{(Array class.)} \(\mathbb M^{(1)}\in\mathcal A_p\) for the treatment \(x=0\) and the allocation sequences \(n_s,n_t\).
\item \textbf{(Separated targets.)} The baseline and row targets satisfy
\[
\theta_{0,1}(\mathcal M^{(0)})=\frac12,
\qquad
\theta_{0,1,n}(\mathcal M^{(1)}_n)=\frac58
\quad\text{for every } n\ge 2 .
\]
\item \textbf{(Contiguous row laws.)} The row laws induced by \(\mathbb M^{(1)}\) and by repeating \(\mathcal M^{(0)}\) along the same allocation sequence satisfy
\[
d_{\mathrm{TV}}\!\left(
\mathbb P_{\mathcal M^{(1)}_n}^{\,n_s(n),n_t(n)},
\mathbb P_{\mathcal M^{(0)}}^{\,n_s(n),n_t(n)}
\right)\longrightarrow 0 .
\]
\end{itemize}
Consequently, for every confidence-set sequence \((\mathcal C_n)_{n\ge 0}\), with each \(\mathcal C_n(\omega)\) nonempty and contained in \([0,1]\), satisfying the uniform array-coverage condition
\[
1-\alpha
\le
\liminf_{n\to\infty}
\inf_{\mathbb M\in\mathcal A_p}
\mathbb P_{\mathcal M_n}^{\,n_s(n),n_t(n)}
\!\left\{
\theta_{0,1,n}(\mathcal M_n)\in\mathcal C_n
\right\},
\]
and for every Wald-localization slack \(\varepsilon\in(0,1/8)\),
\[
1-\alpha
\le
\liminf_{n\to\infty}
\mathbb P_{\mathcal M^{(0)}}^{\,n_s(n),n_t(n)}
\!\left\{
I^W_{n,1-\alpha}\ne\varnothing,\ 
\frac18-\varepsilon
\le
d_H\!\left(\mathcal C_n,I^W_{n,1-\alpha}\right)
\right\}.
\]

a587638f6cc627520dd6dc612a5c83d1163bdfdf.title: Latent-shift factorization
a587638f6cc627520dd6dc612a5c83d1163bdfdf.body:
For every source cell \((e,u,w,x,y)\),
\[
P_{\mathcal M}(e,u,w,x,y)
=
\pi_e S_{ue} M_{wu} a_x(u) f_{x,y}(u,w).
\]

cd748b4af1180dbc0bad00e511bd45b51f36e27c.title: Target mechanism invariance
cd748b4af1180dbc0bad00e511bd45b51f36e27c.body:
For every target cell \((u,w,x,y)\),
\[
Q_{\mathcal M}(u,w,x,y)
=
q_u M_{wu} a_x(u) f_{x,y}(u,w).
\]

5ea1350a0cbe807349424c5e05335a7fa01c6d9d.title: Strict primitive positivity
5ea1350a0cbe807349424c5e05335a7fa01c6d9d.body: Every entry of \(\pi\), \(S\), \(M\), \(a\), \(f\), and \(q\) is strictly positive.

0b595f411da0f00ff24de534c37cd881876651d1.title: Proxy-channel injectivity
0b595f411da0f00ff24de534c37cd881876651d1.body:
The proxy channel \(M\) has full column rank:
\[
\operatorname{rank}(M)=r.
\]

04be0c7c72d9e679e86cf039d2c607defb6afe83.title: Source iid sampling
04be0c7c72d9e679e86cf039d2c607defb6afe83.body: The source observations \(O_1^s,\ldots,O_{n_s}^s\) are independent and identically distributed according to \(P_O\).

241e20d8ea520487c4723693b33c37b1b7310e60.title: Target-proxy iid sampling
241e20d8ea520487c4723693b33c37b1b7310e60.body: The target-proxy observations \(W_1^t,\ldots,W_{n_t}^t\) are independent and identically distributed according to \(b\).

c37dacd741e77a184dfa40c8bbe8c75accee20eb.title: Triangular allocation

1ecca04371ac29d4e7f58719c73ff974d39dd8e5.title: Source row sampling
1ecca04371ac29d4e7f58719c73ff974d39dd8e5.body:
For every \(n\ge 2\), the source observations \((O^s_{1,n},\ldots,O^s_{n_s(n),n})\) are the source coordinate block under the finite row law
\[
\mathbb P_{\mathcal M_n}^{\,n_s(n),n_t(n)}
=
P_{O,n}^{\otimes n_s(n)}\otimes b_n^{\otimes n_t(n)}
\]
on \(\Omega_n\).

5f6c95b503e57f88b42a84a96c2c961d56ce0e2c.title: Target-proxy row sampling
5f6c95b503e57f88b42a84a96c2c961d56ce0e2c.body:
For every \(n\ge 2\), the target proxy observations \((W^t_{1,n},\ldots,W^t_{n_t(n),n})\) are the target coordinate block under the finite row law
\[
\mathbb P_{\mathcal M_n}^{\,n_s(n),n_t(n)}
=
P_{O,n}^{\otimes n_s(n)}\otimes b_n^{\otimes n_t(n)}
\]
on \(\Omega_n\).

43cdfcf4227112cd9e6edd15f68828fddafb0bb5.title: Row-wise target span
43cdfcf4227112cd9e6edd15f68828fddafb0bb5.body:
For every \(n\), the row-\(n\) target proxy law \(b_n\) satisfies
\[
b_n\in\operatorname{col}(B_{x,n}).
\]

ef98763a58ac0c009d1c3a1e30c7d2ddd4496bda.title: Fixed source rank
ef98763a58ac0c009d1c3a1e30c7d2ddd4496bda.body:
The fixed source moment matrix \(H_x\) satisfies
\[
\operatorname{rank}(H_x)=r_0.
\]

d4f9ab3531c78986528d3f72429c5c8651828f33.title: Retained singular gap
d4f9ab3531c78986528d3f72429c5c8651828f33.body:
The retained singular value satisfies
\[
\sigma_{r_0}(H_x)\ge c.
\]

18ec4398dc5e9f14eb2ae1829d874274cf321dda.title: Regular target span
18ec4398dc5e9f14eb2ae1829d874274cf321dda.body:
The fixed target proxy vector lies in the column space of the source moment matrix:
\[
b\in\operatorname{col}(H_x).
\]

15afd5c29f1143a7647fccd4d220c161883febc5.title: Regular cell floor
15afd5c29f1143a7647fccd4d220c161883febc5.body:
The source observed cells and target proxy cells have common lower bound \(\eta\):
\[
\min\bigl(\{P_O(e,w,x,y):e\in\mathcal E,\ w\in\mathcal W,\ x\in\mathcal X,\ y\in\mathcal Y\}\cup\{b_w:w\in\mathcal W\}\bigr)\ge\eta.
\]

485ad5a2c33757a5c7a5f270599ca09324e4b3af.title: Regular positive variance
485ad5a2c33757a5c7a5f270599ca09324e4b3af.body:
The population delta-method variance is bounded below by \(\eta\):
\[
V_{r_0,x,y}(\mathcal M;p)\ge\eta.
\]

b7ecfd98aa69e51f9bbf299c40a242effeb1211a.title: Strictly positive latent-shift class \(\mathfrak M_{+}\)
b7ecfd98aa69e51f9bbf299c40a242effeb1211a.body:
\[
\mathfrak M_{+}
=
\{\mathcal M=(\pi,S,M,a,f,q):
\mathcal M \text{ satisfies } \cref{obj:ass:latent-shift-factorization,obj:ass:target-mechanism-invariance,obj:ass:strict-primitive-positivity}
\text{ and } \operatorname{rank}(M)=r\}.
\]
Here \(r=\lvert\mathcal U\rvert\), the latent cardinality, and the full-column-rank proxy condition is the one in \(\cref{obj:ass:proxy-channel-injectivity}\).

27886b45bc1830f7b321e5e8759d22dc53c6cedc.title: Compatible SCM fiber \(\mathfrak F(\mathcal D)\)
27886b45bc1830f7b321e5e8759d22dc53c6cedc.body:
\[
\mathfrak F(\mathcal D)
=
\{\mathcal M\in\mathfrak M_{+}:
\mathcal M \text{ induces exactly the supplied } P_O \text{ and } b\}.
\]

77f86083f428e39b3a80682dece6ae60e5ce70df.title: Outcome-null perturbation \(f^{(t)}_{x,y}\)
77f86083f428e39b3a80682dece6ae60e5ce70df.body:
For \(\mathcal M\in\mathfrak M_{+}\) as in \(\cref{obj:def:positive-latent-shift-class}\), fix \(h\in\mathcal H_x(\mathcal D)\) as in \(\cref{obj:def:failure-separator}\). Put \(v=M^\top h\), choose \(w_{\star}\in\mathcal W\) and \(y^\circ\ne y\), and define
\[
f^{(t)}_{x,y}(u,w_{\star})
=
f_{x,y}(u,w_{\star})+\frac{t v_u}{M_{w_{\star}u}},
\qquad
f^{(t)}_{x,y^\circ}(u,w_{\star})
=
f_{x,y^\circ}(u,w_{\star})-\frac{t v_u}{M_{w_{\star}u}}.
\]
Every other cell of \(f^{(t)}\) equals the corresponding cell of \(f\).

558427496a9f25ff89097d3ae2f5d6bb4e773fb2.title: Rank-deficient witness \(\mathcal M^{\star}\)
558427496a9f25ff89097d3ae2f5d6bb4e773fb2.body:
The SCM \(\mathcal M^{\star}\) is specified by
\[
\mathcal E=\{e_1,e_2\},\qquad
\mathcal U=\mathcal W=\{0,1,2\},\qquad
\mathcal X=\mathcal Y=\{0,1\},
\]
\[
\pi=(1/2,1/2),\qquad
S=
\begin{pmatrix}
9/19 & 1/12\\
2/19 & 2/3\\
8/19 & 1/4
\end{pmatrix},
\]
\[
a_1=(1/10,3/5,1/5)^\top,\qquad
a_0=\mathbf 1-a_1,
\]
with \(M\) having diagonal entries \(4/5\) and off-diagonal entries \(1/10\), and
\[
q=(1197,2436,2204)^\top/5837.
\]
For \(i,j\in\{0,1,2\}\) and \(x\in\{0,1\}\),
\[
f_{x,1}(u_i,w_j)=\frac15+\frac{x}{5}+\frac{i}{20}+\frac{j}{100},
\qquad
f_{x,0}(u_i,w_j)=1-f_{x,1}(u_i,w_j).
\]

405a87b18863bc5684145957afa20b05fd6e7ef7.title: Projection set \(\widehat C_{x,y,1-\alpha}\)
405a87b18863bc5684145957afa20b05fd6e7ef7.body:
Let
\[
L=m\lvert\mathcal E\rvert+\lvert\mathcal E\rvert+m,
\qquad
r_s=\sqrt{\frac{\log(2L/\alpha)}{2n_s}},
\qquad
r_t=\sqrt{\frac{\log(2L/\alpha)}{2n_t}}.
\]
Define
\[
\widehat C_{x,y,1-\alpha}
=
\left\{
\vartheta\in[0,1]:
\exists \kappa\in\mathbb R^{\lvert\mathcal E\rvert}
\text{ such that }
\lVert \widehat H_x\kappa-\widehat b\rVert_{\infty}
\le
r_s\lVert\kappa\rVert_1+r_t
\text{ and }
\left|\widehat z_{x,y}^{\top}\kappa-\vartheta\right|
\le
r_s\lVert\kappa\rVert_1
\right\}.
\]

6e136b5b7b725e449ab40d2e3017c526fc7bd588.title: Fixed-allocation array class \(\mathcal A_p\)
6e136b5b7b725e449ab40d2e3017c526fc7bd588.body:
Fix \(p\in(0,1)\) and a deterministic allocation sequence \((n_s(n),n_t(n))_{n\ge2}\) satisfying \(\cref{obj:ass:triangular-allocation}\). Relative to this sequence, and under \(\cref{obj:ass:triangular-source-iid-sampling,obj:ass:triangular-target-iid-sampling,obj:ass:array-target-span}\), define
\[
\mathcal A_p
=
\left\{
\mathbb M=(\mathcal M_n)_{n\ge2}:
\begin{array}{l}
\text{for every } n\ge2,\ 
\mathbb P_{\mathcal M_n}^{\,n_s(n),n_t(n)}
=
P_{O,n}^{\otimes n_s(n)}\otimes b_n^{\otimes n_t(n)}
\text{ on } \Omega_n=\Omega(n_s(n),n_t(n)),\\
\text{and } b_n\in\operatorname{col}(B_{x,n})
\end{array}
\right\}.
\]
The class allows row-wise changes in \(\operatorname{rank}(B_{x,n})\), singular joint multinomial covariance, and divergent balancing-weight norm \(d_{x,n}\).

b88923dd978b2b8a813f42819a30d5ca953c68e1.title: Strongly identified submodel \(\mathcal R_{r_0,c,\eta}\)
b88923dd978b2b8a813f42819a30d5ca953c68e1.body:
For \(1\le r_0\le\min(m,\lvert\mathcal E\rvert)\) and fixed \(c,\eta>0\), define \(\mathcal R_{r_0,c,\eta}\) as the set of all \(\mathcal M\in\mathfrak M_{+}\) satisfying \(\cref{obj:def:positive-latent-shift-class,obj:ass:regular-fixed-rank,obj:ass:regular-singular-gap,obj:ass:regular-target-span,obj:ass:regular-cell-floor,obj:ass:regular-positive-variance}\) through the following conditions:
\[
\mathcal R_{r_0,c,\eta}
=
\left\{
\mathcal M\in\mathfrak M_{+}:
\begin{array}{l}
\operatorname{rank}(H_x)=r_0,\\
\sigma_{r_0}(H_x)\ge c,\\
b\in\operatorname{col}(H_x),\\
\text{every source and target cell is at least }\eta,\\
V_{r_0,x,y}(\mathcal M;p)\ge\eta
\end{array}
\right\}.
\]

918348ed9e382882e9ca17e7f450c0c911bf250d.title: Wald functional \(\phi_{r_0}(H,z,b)\)
918348ed9e382882e9ca17e7f450c0c911bf250d.body:
For \(H\in\mathbb R^{m\times\lvert\mathcal E\rvert}\), \(z\in\mathbb R^{\lvert\mathcal E\rvert}\), and \(b\in\mathbb R^m\), define
\[
\phi_{r_0}(H,z,b)=z^{\top}H_{r_0}^{\dagger}b,
\]
where \(H_{r_0}=H^{\star}_{r_0}\) is the selector-based Gram-spectral truncation of \(H\). The selector fixes a single value of \(\phi_{r_0}\) at tied cutoffs. If
\[
\sigma_{r_0}(H)>\sigma_{r_0+1}(H),
\]
then the retained subspace is unique, and \(H_{r_0}\) and \(\phi_{r_0}(H,z,b)\) are independent of the fixed within-tie selector.

a2d8c01169a0621f3cfbc8496536224d9eec7c46.title: Wald estimator \(\widehat\theta^{\,W}_{x,y,n}\)
a2d8c01169a0621f3cfbc8496536224d9eec7c46.body:
Define the truncated-SVD Wald estimator by
\[
\widehat\theta^{\,W}_{x,y,n}
=
\phi_{r_0}(\widehat H_{x,n},\widehat z_{x,y,n},\widehat b_n).
\]

46a98063276933ca07b00beffbe9c79a5e74bb26.title: Wald variance \(\widehat V_n\)
46a98063276933ca07b00beffbe9c79a5e74bb26.body:
Put
\[
\widehat T_n=(\widehat H_{x,n},\widehat z_{x,y,n},\widehat b_n).
\]
Let \(\widehat\Gamma_n\) be the plug-in covariance matrix of \(\sqrt n\,\widehat T_n\), formed from the joint source multinomial covariance and the target multinomial covariance with allocation factors \(p^{-1}\) and \((1-p)^{-1}\). Define the totalized plug-in variance by
\[
\widehat V_n=
\begin{cases}
D\phi_{r_0}(\widehat T_n)\,\widehat\Gamma_n\,D\phi_{r_0}(\widehat T_n)^{\top},
&\sigma_{r_0}(\widehat H_{x,n})>\sigma_{r_0+1}(\widehat H_{x,n}),\\
0,&\sigma_{r_0}(\widehat H_{x,n})\le\sigma_{r_0+1}(\widehat H_{x,n}),
\end{cases}
\]
where \(D\phi_{r_0}\) is the ordinary derivative of the selector-independent functional on the strict-cutoff-gap region, and where
\[
\sigma_{\bar q+1}=0,
\qquad
\bar q=\min(m,\lvert\mathcal E\rvert).
\]
The second line is the fixed nonnegative fallback.

c1f246382913049a4769d6bce5fcf67ba05b4bfe.title: Wald interval \(I^W_{n,1-\alpha}\)

f8a34897ed67b67114f97bf51e54534379c31536.title: Euclidean diameter \(\operatorname{diam}_2(C)\)
f8a34897ed67b67114f97bf51e54534379c31536.body:
For \(C\subseteq[0,1]\), define
\[
\operatorname{diam}_2(C)=\sup_{\xi,\zeta\in C}|\xi-\zeta|,
\]
with the convention \(\operatorname{diam}_2(\varnothing)=0\).

3afa3bdf424eadf4337c789461af9131c6c97500.title: Euclidean Hausdorff distance \(d_H(C,D)\)
3afa3bdf424eadf4337c789461af9131c6c97500.body:
For nonempty \(C,D\subseteq[0,1]\), define the Euclidean Hausdorff distance by
\[
d_H(C,D)=
\max\left\{
\sup_{\xi\in C}\inf_{\zeta\in D}|\xi-\zeta|,
\sup_{\zeta\in D}\inf_{\xi\in C}|\xi-\zeta|
\right\}.
\]

3697551dd1e7fbb4248c1edd2d09489f03692df3.title: No uniform Wald adaptation
3697551dd1e7fbb4248c1edd2d09489f03692df3.body:
Fix a source allocation limit \(p\in(0,1)\), an error level \(\alpha\in(0,1)\), and deterministic allocation sequences \(n_s(n)\) and \(n_t(n)\) satisfying \cref{obj:ass:triangular-allocation}. For each row \(n\), write \(\Omega_n=\Omega(n_s(n),n_t(n))\). For a two-sample array \(\mathbb M=(\mathcal M_n)_{n\ge0}\), define the row-\(n\) target interventional probability by
\[
\theta_{x,y,n}(\mathbb M)=\theta_{x,y}(\mathcal M_n)
=\sum_{u,w} q_n(u)M_n(w\mid u)f_{n,x,y}(u,w).
\]
Then there exist a fixed latent-shift SCM \(\mathcal M^{(0)}\) with binary \(\mathcal E,\mathcal U,\mathcal W,\mathcal Y\) and singleton \(\mathcal X\), and a two-sample triangular array \(\mathbb M^{(1)}=(\mathcal M^{(1)}_n)_{n\ge0}\) on the same state spaces and allocation sequences, such that:
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Regular baseline.)} \(\mathcal M^{(0)}\) belongs to the strongly identified regular submodel \(\mathcal R_{1,1/4,1/16}\) at treatment \(x=0\), outcome \(y=1\), and source allocation limit \(p\).
\item \textbf{(Array class.)} \(\mathbb M^{(1)}\) belongs to the studentized fixed-allocation changing-rank array class \(\mathcal A_p\) at treatment \(x=0\) and allocation sequences \(n_s,n_t\).
\item \textbf{(Separated targets.)} The baseline target and row targets satisfy
\[
\theta_{0,1}(\mathcal M^{(0)})=\frac12,
\qquad
\theta_{0,1,n}(\mathbb M^{(1)})=\frac58
\quad\text{for every } n\ge2 .
\]
\item \textbf{(Contiguous row laws.)} The row law of \(\mathbb M^{(1)}\) and the row law obtained by repeating \(\mathcal M^{(0)}\) along the same allocation sequence satisfy
\[
d_{\mathrm{TV}}\!\left(
\mathbb P_{\mathcal M^{(1)}_n}^{\,n_s(n),n_t(n)},
\mathbb P_{\mathcal M^{(0)}}^{\,n_s(n),n_t(n)}
\right)\longrightarrow 0 .
\]
\end{itemize}
Consequently, for every confidence-set sequence \((\mathcal C_n)_{n\ge0}\), with each \(\mathcal C_n(\omega)\) nonempty and contained in \([0,1]\), satisfying the uniform array-coverage condition
\[
1-\alpha
\le
\liminf_{n\to\infty}
\inf_{\mathbb M\in\mathcal A_p}
\mathbb P_{\mathcal M_n}^{\,n_s(n),n_t(n)}
\!\left\{
\theta_{0,1,n}(\mathbb M)\in\mathcal C_n
\right\},
\]
and for every Wald-localization slack \(\varepsilon\in(0,1/8)\), the rank-one studentized Wald interval \(I^W_{n,1-\alpha}(\omega)\) computed at \(\mathcal M^{(0)}\), treatment \(x=0\), outcome \(y=1\), allocation limit \(p\), and allocation sequences \(n_s,n_t\) satisfies
\[
1-\alpha
\le
\liminf_{n\to\infty}
\mathbb P_{\mathcal M^{(0)}}^{\,n_s(n),n_t(n)}
\!\left\{
I^W_{n,1-\alpha}\ne\varnothing,\ 
\frac18-\varepsilon
\le
d_H\!\left(\mathcal C_n,I^W_{n,1-\alpha}\right)
\right\}.
\]

ee183b1741dd3815fb575cbf6067a458325be9e2.title: Row-wise target span
ee183b1741dd3815fb575cbf6067a458325be9e2.body:
For every \(n\), let \(B_{x,n}\) denote the row-\(n\) conditional proxy matrix with entries
\[
B_{x,n}(w,e)=P_{O,n}(W=w\mid E=e,X=x).
\]
The row-\(n\) target proxy law satisfies
\[
b_n\in\operatorname{col}(B_{x,n}).
\]

01bb9586a24a571f6515d8a968d12cd56cb01d9f.title: Positive Wald variance
01bb9586a24a571f6515d8a968d12cd56cb01d9f.body:
Let
\[
T(\mathcal M)=(H_x,z_{x,y},b),
\]
let \(\Gamma(\mathcal M;p)\) be the covariance matrix of the allocation-scaled empirical moment tuple corresponding to source allocation limit \(p\), and let \(D\phi_{r_0}(T(\mathcal M))\) be the derivative of the rank-\(r_0\) truncated-SVD Wald functional at \(T(\mathcal M)\). Define the population delta-method variance by
\[
V_{r_0,x,y}(\mathcal M;p)
=
D\phi_{r_0}(T(\mathcal M))\,
\Gamma(\mathcal M;p)\,
D\phi_{r_0}(T(\mathcal M))^{\top}.
\]
It satisfies
\[
V_{r_0,x,y}(\mathcal M;p)\ge\eta.
\]

1dea85dea6edb6c8d5eabc6eec2afa51d32efa28.title: Array class \(\mathcal A_p\)
1dea85dea6edb6c8d5eabc6eec2afa51d32efa28.body:
Fix \(p\in(0,1)\) and a deterministic allocation sequence \((n_s(n),n_t(n))_{n\ge2}\) satisfying \cref{obj:ass:triangular-allocation}. Relative to this sequence, and under \cref{obj:ass:triangular-source-iid-sampling,obj:ass:triangular-target-iid-sampling,obj:ass:array-target-span}, define the finite two-sample product sample space by
\[
\Omega(n_s,n_t)
=
\mathcal O_s^{\,n_s}\times \mathcal W^{\,n_t},
\]
and set
\[
\Omega_n=\Omega(n_s(n),n_t(n)).
\]
For each row \(n\), define the minimum balancing-weight norm by
\[
d_{x,n}
=
\inf\left\{\|\lambda\|_2:\lambda\in\mathbb R^{\lvert\mathcal E\rvert},\ B_{x,n}\lambda=b_n\right\}.
\]
The fixed-allocation changing-rank array class is
\[
\mathcal A_p
=
\left\{
\mathbb M=(\mathcal M_n)_{n\ge2}:
\begin{array}{l}
\text{for every } n\ge2,\ 
\mathbb P_{\mathcal M_n}^{\,n_s(n),n_t(n)}
=
P_{O,n}^{\otimes n_s(n)}\otimes b_n^{\otimes n_t(n)}
\text{ on } \Omega_n,\\
\text{and } b_n\in\operatorname{col}(B_{x,n})
\end{array}
\right\}.
\]
The class allows row-wise changes in \(\operatorname{rank}(B_{x,n})\), singular joint multinomial covariance, and divergent balancing-weight norm \(d_{x,n}\).

15369aacfb187411e171048a3f5238afe1c9cc38.title: Wald interval \(I^W_{n,1-\alpha}\)
15369aacfb187411e171048a3f5238afe1c9cc38.body:
Let \(\Phi\) denote the standard-normal distribution function, and define the standard-normal \((1-\alpha/2)\)-quantile by
\[
z_{1-\alpha/2}
=
\Phi^{-1}(1-\alpha/2).
\]
Define the truncated-SVD Wald interval by
\[
I^W_{n,1-\alpha}
=
\left[
\widehat\theta^{\,W}_{x,y,n}
\pm
z_{1-\alpha/2}\sqrt{\widehat V_n/n}
\right]\cap[0,1].
\]

955174850e13e1fa983d914eb557069de0b9cc76.title: Observable law factorization
955174850e13e1fa983d914eb557069de0b9cc76.body:
Let \(\mathcal M\) be a normalized finite latent-shift SCM on finite state spaces \(\mathcal E,\mathcal U,\mathcal W,\mathcal X,\mathcal Y\), and suppose that \(\mathcal M\in\mathfrak M_{+}\) in the sense of \cref{obj:def:positive-latent-shift-class}. For \(x\in\mathcal X\) and \(y\in\mathcal Y\), define the latent posterior matrix \(R_x\), the conditional outcome vector \(c_{x,y}\), the latent-proxy averaged outcome vector \(g_{x,y}\), and the target interventional probability \(\theta_{x,y}\) by
\[
R_x(u,e)=\frac{a_x(u)S(u,e)}{\rho_x(e)},\qquad
c_{x,y}(e)=\frac{\sum_{w\in\mathcal W}P_O(e,w,x,y)}
{\sum_{w\in\mathcal W}\sum_{y'\in\mathcal Y}P_O(e,w,x,y')},
\]
\[
g_{x,y}(u)=\sum_{w\in\mathcal W}M(w,u)f_{x,y}(u,w),\qquad
\theta_{x,y}=\sum_{u\in\mathcal U}\sum_{w\in\mathcal W}q(u)M(w,u)f_{x,y}(u,w).
\]
Then
\[
B_x=MR_x,\qquad
b=Mq,\qquad
c_{x,y}=g_{x,y}^{\top}R_x,\qquad
\theta_{x,y}=g_{x,y}^{\top}q .
\]
Moreover, for every \(\lambda\in\Lambda_x(\mathcal D)\), with \(\Lambda_x(\mathcal D)\) as in \cref{obj:def:balancing-fiber}, the unconditional weight \(\kappa\) induced by \(\lambda\) as in \cref{obj:def:unconditional-weight-map} satisfies
\[
H_x\kappa=b
\qquad\text{and}\qquad
z_{x,y}^{\top}\kappa=\theta_{x,y}.
\]
Finally, there exists a vector \(h:\mathcal W\to\mathbb R\) such that
\[
H_x^{\top}h=z_{x,y}.
\]

b3ebb00d396a2c2b578b930c8dcf787dac728f3e.title: No uniform Wald adaptation
b3ebb00d396a2c2b578b930c8dcf787dac728f3e.body:
Fix a source allocation limit \(p\in(0,1)\), an error level \(\alpha\in(0,1)\), and deterministic allocation sequences \(n_s(n)\) and \(n_t(n)\) satisfying \cref{obj:ass:triangular-allocation}. For each \(n\), write \(\Omega_n=\Omega(n_s(n),n_t(n))\). Then there exist a fixed latent-shift SCM \(\mathcal M^{(0)}\) with \(\mathcal E=\mathcal U=\mathcal W=\mathcal Y=\{0,1\}\) and singleton treatment space \(\mathcal X=\{0\}\), and a two-sample triangular array \(\mathbb M^{(1)}=(\mathcal M^{(1)}_n)_{n\ge 0}\) on the same state spaces and allocation sequences, such that:
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Regular baseline.)} \(\mathcal M^{(0)}\in\mathcal R_{1,1/4,1/16}\) for treatment \(0\), outcome \(1\), and source allocation limit \(p\).
\item \textbf{(Array class.)} \(\mathbb M^{(1)}\in\mathcal A_p\) for treatment \(0\) and the allocation sequences \(n_s,n_t\).
\item \textbf{(Separated targets.)} The baseline and row targets satisfy
\[
\theta_{0,1}(\mathcal M^{(0)})=\frac12,
\qquad
\theta_{0,1,n}(\mathcal M^{(1)}_n)=\frac58
\quad\text{for every } n\ge 2 .
\]
\item \textbf{(Contiguous row laws.)} The row laws induced by \(\mathbb M^{(1)}\) and by repeating \(\mathcal M^{(0)}\) along the same allocation sequence satisfy
\[
d_{\mathrm{TV}}\!\left(
\mathbb P_{\mathcal M^{(1)}_n}^{\,n_s(n),n_t(n)},
\mathbb P_{\mathcal M^{(0)}}^{\,n_s(n),n_t(n)}
\right)\longrightarrow 0 .
\]
\end{itemize}
Consequently, for every confidence-set sequence \((\mathcal C_n)_{n\ge 0}\), with each reported set nonempty and contained in \([0,1]\), satisfying
\[
1-\alpha
\le
\liminf_{n\to\infty}
\inf_{\mathbb M\in\mathcal A_p}
\mathbb P_{\mathcal M_n}^{\,n_s(n),n_t(n)}
\!\left\{
\theta_{0,1,n}(\mathcal M_n)\in\mathcal C_n
\right\},
\]
and for every Wald-localization slack \(\varepsilon\in(0,1/8)\), the rank-one Wald interval \(I^W_{n,1-\alpha}(\omega)\) computed at \(\mathcal M^{(0)}\), treatment \(0\), outcome \(1\), source allocation limit \(p\), allocation sequences \(n_s,n_t\), and nominal level \(\alpha\) satisfies
\[
1-\alpha
\le
\liminf_{n\to\infty}
\mathbb P_{\mathcal M^{(0)}}^{\,n_s(n),n_t(n)}
\!\left\{
I^W_{n,1-\alpha}\ne\varnothing,\ 
\frac18-\varepsilon
\le
d_H\!\left(\mathcal C_n,I^W_{n,1-\alpha}\right)
\right\}.
\]

3c0d74061de22e5e2924175aa8b85f66e4720584.title: Source iid sampling
3c0d74061de22e5e2924175aa8b85f66e4720584.body:
Let \(P_O\), the observed source law, be the marginal of the full-data law \(P_{\mathcal M}\):
\[
P_O(e,w,x,y)
=
\sum_{u\in\mathcal U} P_{\mathcal M}(e,u,w,x,y).
\]
The source observations \(O_1^s,\ldots,O_{n_s}^s\) are independent and identically distributed according to \(P_O\).

e822f9bd32f61692e37a14d06767b87f22d41579.title: Target proxy sampling
e822f9bd32f61692e37a14d06767b87f22d41579.body:
Let \(b\), the target proxy law, be the \(\mathcal W\)-marginal of the target law \(Q_{\mathcal M}\):
\[
b(w)=Q_{\mathcal M}(W=w).
\]
The target-proxy observations \(W_1^t,\ldots,W_{n_t}^t\) are independent and identically distributed according to \(b\).

46212a77335560a2b5d6c92f20753b28eb7e3e37.title: Fixed rank condition
46212a77335560a2b5d6c92f20753b28eb7e3e37.body:
Let \(H_x\), the unconditional source moment matrix, have entries
\[
H_x(w,e)=P_O(E=e,W=w,X=x).
\]
The fixed source moment matrix \(H_x\) satisfies
\[
\operatorname{rank}(H_x)=r_0.
\]

5337473494bc69c60f9e8cffb2f7fcf48aeffc08.title: Positive Wald variance
5337473494bc69c60f9e8cffb2f7fcf48aeffc08.body:
Let \(z_{x,y}\), the unconditional source outcome-moment vector, have entries
\[
z_{x,y}(e)=P_O(E=e,X=x,Y=y).
\]
Let \(V_{r_0,x,y}(\mathcal M;p)\) denote the population delta-method variance of the retained-rank Wald functional \(\phi_{r_0}\) under source allocation limit \(p\). The variance satisfies
\[
V_{r_0,x,y}(\mathcal M;p)\ge\eta.
\]

0eaf5bae26d8b4879e30300a281637f0b18aa187.title: Balancing fiber \(\Lambda_x(\mathcal D)\)
0eaf5bae26d8b4879e30300a281637f0b18aa187.body:
Let \(B_x\), the source conditional proxy matrix, have entries
\[
B_x(w,e)=P_O(W=w\mid E=e,X=x).
\]
The balancing fiber is
\[
\Lambda_x(\mathcal D)
=
\{\lambda\in\mathbb R^{\lvert\mathcal E\rvert}:B_x\lambda=b\}.
\]

6fbc8a0aa46bb9910662100bf9286349b1919df6.title: Projection set \(\widehat C_{x,y,1-\alpha}\)
6fbc8a0aa46bb9910662100bf9286349b1919df6.body:
Let \(\widehat H_x\), the empirical source moment matrix, have entries
\[
\widehat H_x(w,e)
=
\frac{1}{n_s}\sum_{i=1}^{n_s}\mathbf 1\{E_i^s=e,W_i^s=w,X_i^s=x\}.
\]
Let \(\widehat z_{x,y}\), the empirical source outcome-moment vector, have entries
\[
\widehat z_{x,y}(e)
=
\frac{1}{n_s}\sum_{i=1}^{n_s}\mathbf 1\{E_i^s=e,X_i^s=x,Y_i^s=y\}.
\]
Let \(\widehat b\), the empirical target-proxy vector, have entries
\[
\widehat b(w)
=
\frac{1}{n_t}\sum_{j=1}^{n_t}\mathbf 1\{W_j^t=w\}.
\]
Let
\[
L=m\lvert\mathcal E\rvert+\lvert\mathcal E\rvert+m,
\qquad
r_s=\sqrt{\frac{\log(2L/\alpha)}{2n_s}},
\qquad
r_t=\sqrt{\frac{\log(2L/\alpha)}{2n_t}}.
\]
The concentration-calibrated projection confidence set is
\[
\widehat C_{x,y,1-\alpha}
=
\left\{
\vartheta\in[0,1]:
\exists \kappa\in\mathbb R^{\lvert\mathcal E\rvert}
\text{ such that }
\lVert \widehat H_x\kappa-\widehat b\rVert_{\infty}
\le
r_s\lVert\kappa\rVert_1+r_t
\text{ and }
\left|\widehat z_{x,y}^{\top}\kappa-\vartheta\right|
\le
r_s\lVert\kappa\rVert_1
\right\}.
\]

59cf8ba43efb5d14dfd255a09c331a8fcf698325.title: Array class \(\mathcal A_p\) and norm \(d_{x,n}\)
59cf8ba43efb5d14dfd255a09c331a8fcf698325.body:
Fix \(p\in(0,1)\) and a deterministic allocation sequence \((n_s(n),n_t(n))_{n\ge2}\) satisfying \cref{obj:ass:triangular-allocation}. Relative to this sequence, and under \cref{obj:ass:triangular-source-iid-sampling,obj:ass:triangular-target-iid-sampling,obj:ass:array-target-span}, define
\[
\mathcal A_p
=
\left\{
\mathbb M=(\mathcal M_n)_{n\ge2}:
\begin{array}{l}
\text{for every } n\ge2,\ 
\mathbb P_{\mathcal M_n}^{\,n_s(n),n_t(n)}
=
P_{O,n}^{\otimes n_s(n)}\otimes b_n^{\otimes n_t(n)}
\text{ on } \Omega_n=\Omega(n_s(n),n_t(n)),\\
\text{and } b_n\in\operatorname{col}(B_{x,n})
\end{array}
\right\}.
\]
For each row \(n\), define the minimum balancing-weight norm by
\[
d_{x,n}
=
\min\left\{
\|\lambda\|_2:
\lambda\in\mathbb R^{|\mathcal E|},
\ B_{x,n}\lambda=b_n
\right\}.
\]
The class allows row-wise changes in \(\operatorname{rank}(B_{x,n})\), singular joint multinomial covariance, and divergent \(d_{x,n}\).

34532e7fe0ecb80f50c1ffc59302f55fedf932e7.title: Wald estimator \(\widehat\theta^{\,W}_{x,y,n}\)
34532e7fe0ecb80f50c1ffc59302f55fedf932e7.body:
For row \(n\), define the empirical source moment matrix, empirical source outcome-moment vector, and empirical target-proxy vector by
\[
\widehat H_{x,n}(w,e)
=
\frac{1}{n_s(n)}
\sum_{i=1}^{n_s(n)}
\mathbf 1\{E_i^s=e,\ W_i^s=w,\ X_i^s=x\},
\]
\[
\widehat z_{x,y,n}(e)
=
\frac{1}{n_s(n)}
\sum_{i=1}^{n_s(n)}
\mathbf 1\{E_i^s=e,\ X_i^s=x,\ Y_i^s=y\},
\]
and
\[
\widehat b_n(w)
=
\frac{1}{n_t(n)}
\sum_{j=1}^{n_t(n)}
\mathbf 1\{W_j^t=w\}.
\]
Define the truncated-SVD Wald estimator by
\[
\widehat\theta^{\,W}_{x,y,n}
=
\phi_{r_0}(\widehat H_{x,n},\widehat z_{x,y,n},\widehat b_n).
\]

a898702bb34679c11471acfb31ae1f6ce2814372.title: Observable factorization
a898702bb34679c11471acfb31ae1f6ce2814372.body:
Let \(\mathcal M\) be a latent-shift SCM on finite state spaces \(\mathcal E,\mathcal U,\mathcal W,\mathcal X,\mathcal Y\), and suppose that \(\mathcal M\in\mathfrak M_{+}\) in the sense of \cref{obj:def:positive-latent-shift-class}. For each \(x\in\mathcal X\), let \(\rho_x(e)\) be the source treatment probability in environment \(e\), and define the latent posterior matrix and latent-proxy averaged outcome vector by
\[
R_x(u,e)=\frac{a_x(u)S(u,e)}{\rho_x(e)},
\qquad
g_{x,y}(u)=\sum_{w\in\mathcal W}M(w,u)f_{x,y}(u,w).
\]
Then, for every \(x\in\mathcal X\) and \(y\in\mathcal Y\),
\[
B_x = M R_x,\qquad
b = Mq,\qquad
c_{x,y}=g_{x,y}^{\top}R_x,\qquad
\theta_{x,y}=g_{x,y}^{\top}q .
\]
Moreover, for every \(\lambda\in\Lambda_x(\mathcal D)\) in \cref{obj:def:balancing-fiber}, the unconditional weight \(\kappa\) induced by \(\lambda\) as in \cref{obj:def:unconditional-weight-map} satisfies
\[
H_x\kappa=b
\qquad\text{and}\qquad
z_{x,y}^{\top}\kappa=\theta_{x,y}.
\]
Finally, there exists a vector \(h:\mathcal W\to\mathbb R\) such that
\[
H_x^{\top}h=z_{x,y}.
\]

6755282386a6ab33ff909c4bc233cc95077bbcd9.title: Finite-sample projection coverage
6755282386a6ab33ff909c4bc233cc95077bbcd9.body:
Let \(\mathcal M\) be a latent-shift SCM on finite state spaces \(\mathcal E,\mathcal U,\mathcal W,\mathcal X,\mathcal Y\), let \(P_O\) be an observed source law, and let \(b\) be a target proxy law. Fix \(x\in\mathcal X\) and \(y\in\mathcal Y\). Suppose that
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Positive latent shift.)} \(\mathcal M\in\mathfrak M_{+}\) in the sense of \cref{obj:def:positive-latent-shift-class}.
\item \textbf{(Compatibility.)} \(\mathcal M\in\mathfrak F(\mathcal D)\), with \(\mathcal D=(P_O,b)\), in the sense of \cref{obj:def:compatible-fiber}.
\item \textbf{(Balancing feasibility.)} The affine balancing set \(\Lambda_x(\mathcal D)\) from \cref{obj:def:balancing-fiber} is nonempty; equivalently, there exists \(\lambda:\mathcal E\to\mathbb R\) such that \(B_x\lambda=b\).
\item \textbf{(Sample sizes and level.)} The sample sizes satisfy \(n_s>0\) and \(n_t>0\), and the nominal error level satisfies \(0<\alpha<1\).
\end{itemize}
Let \(\mathbb P_{\mathcal M}^{\,n_s,n_t}\) denote the fixed-model two-sample product law
\[
\mathbb P_{\mathcal M}^{\,n_s,n_t}
=
\left(\bigotimes_{i=1}^{n_s} P_{O,\mathcal M}\right)
\otimes
\left(\bigotimes_{j=1}^{n_t} b_{\mathcal M}\right),
\]
where \(P_{O,\mathcal M}\) is the observed source law induced by \(\mathcal M\) on \(\mathcal E\times\mathcal W\times\mathcal X\times\mathcal Y\) and \(b_{\mathcal M}\) is the target proxy law induced by \(\mathcal M\) on \(\mathcal W\). Then
\[
1-\alpha
\le
\mathbb P_{\mathcal M}^{\,n_s,n_t}
\left\{
\theta_{x,y}\in
\widehat C_{x,y,1-\alpha}
\right\}.
\]
Here
\[
\theta_{x,y}
=
\sum_{u\in\mathcal U}\sum_{w\in\mathcal W}
q(u)M(w,u)f_{x,y}(u,w),
\]
and \(\widehat C_{x,y,1-\alpha}\) is the concentration-calibrated projection set of \cref{obj:def:concentration-projection-set} formed from \(\widehat H_x\), \(\widehat z_{x,y}\), \(\widehat b\), \(n_s\), \(n_t\), and \(\alpha\).

e2fb941bf2f87e4d7e3bca62181a0f4c2b422a46.title: Uniform Wald separation
e2fb941bf2f87e4d7e3bca62181a0f4c2b422a46.body:
Fix a source allocation limit \(p\in(0,1)\), an error level \(\alpha\in(0,1)\), and deterministic allocation sequences \(n_s(n)\) and \(n_t(n)\) satisfying \cref{obj:ass:triangular-allocation}. For each row \(n\), write \(\Omega_n=\Omega(n_s(n),n_t(n))\), and for any row model \(\mathcal M_n\) define the row-wise target interventional probability by
\[
\theta_{0,1,n}(\mathcal M_n)
=
\sum_{u}\sum_{w} q_n(u) M_n(w\mid u) f_{0,1,n}(u,w).
\]
Then there exist a fixed latent-shift SCM \(\mathcal M^{(0)}\) with binary \(\mathcal E,\mathcal U,\mathcal W,\mathcal Y\) and singleton \(\mathcal X\), and a two-sample triangular array \(\mathbb M^{(1)}=(\mathcal M^{(1)}_n)_{n\ge0}\) on the same state spaces and allocation sequences, such that:
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Regular baseline.)} \(\mathcal M^{(0)}\in\mathcal R_{1,1/4,1/16}\) for treatment \(0\), outcome \(1\), and source allocation limit \(p\).
\item \textbf{(Array class.)} \(\mathbb M^{(1)}\in\mathcal A_p\) for treatment \(0\) and allocation sequences \(n_s,n_t\).
\item \textbf{(Separated targets.)} The baseline and row targets satisfy
\[
\theta_{0,1}(\mathcal M^{(0)})=\frac12,
\qquad
\theta_{0,1,n}(\mathcal M^{(1)}_n)=\frac58
\quad\text{for every } n\ge2 .
\]
\item \textbf{(Contiguous row laws.)} The row laws induced by \(\mathbb M^{(1)}\) and by repeating \(\mathcal M^{(0)}\) along the same allocation sequence satisfy
\[
d_{\mathrm{TV}}\!\left(
\mathbb P_{\mathcal M^{(1)}_n}^{\,n_s(n),n_t(n)},
\mathbb P_{\mathcal M^{(0)}}^{\,n_s(n),n_t(n)}
\right)
\longrightarrow 0 .
\]
\end{itemize}
Consequently, for every confidence-set sequence \((\mathcal C_n)_{n\ge0}\), with each reported set nonempty and contained in \([0,1]\), satisfying
\[
1-\alpha
\le
\liminf_{n\to\infty}
\inf_{\mathbb M\in\mathcal A_p}
\mathbb P_{\mathcal M_n}^{\,n_s(n),n_t(n)}
\!\left\{
\theta_{0,1,n}(\mathcal M_n)\in\mathcal C_n
\right\},
\]
and for every Wald-localization slack \(\varepsilon\in(0,1/8)\),
\[
1-\alpha
\le
\liminf_{n\to\infty}
\mathbb P_{\mathcal M^{(0)}}^{\,n_s(n),n_t(n)}
\!\left(E_n(\varepsilon)\right),
\]
where \(E_n(\varepsilon)=\Omega_n\) for \(n<2\), while for \(n\ge2\),
\[
E_n(\varepsilon)
=
\left\{
\omega\in\Omega_n:
I^W_{n,1-\alpha}(\omega)\ne\varnothing,\
\frac18-\varepsilon
\le
d_H\!\left(\mathcal C_n(\omega),I^W_{n,1-\alpha}(\omega)\right)
\right\}.
\]

16c6e0a2aa5bed72f85ccd7aa73d3d8f67c69537.title: Source iid sampling
16c6e0a2aa5bed72f85ccd7aa73d3d8f67c69537.body:
Let \(P_O\) denote the observed source marginal law induced by \(P_{\mathcal M}\), with
\[
P_O(e,w,x,y)
=
\sum_{u\in\mathcal U}
\pi(e)S(u\mid e)M(w\mid u)a_x(u)f_{x,y}(u,w).
\]
The source observations \(O_1^s,\ldots,O_{n_s}^s\) are independent and identically distributed according to \(P_O\).

b2595b488d8f0e14beedda5fa2da3826a5835d05.title: Target-proxy iid sampling
b2595b488d8f0e14beedda5fa2da3826a5835d05.body:
Let \(b\) denote the target proxy marginal law, with
\[
b(w)=\sum_{u\in\mathcal U}q(u)M(w\mid u).
\]
The target-proxy observations \(W_1^t,\ldots,W_{n_t}^t\) are independent and identically distributed according to \(b\).

b79f88d1abb6130e51fb9f970a3648a7d2696722.title: Positive Wald variance
b79f88d1abb6130e51fb9f970a3648a7d2696722.body:
Let \(V_{r_0,x,y}(\mathcal M;p)\) denote the population delta-method variance of the retained-rank Wald functional \(\phi_{r_0}\) under source allocation limit \(p\):
\[
V_{r_0,x,y}(\mathcal M;p)
=
\operatorname{Var}_{\mathcal M,p}
\!\left(
D\phi_{r_0}(H_x,z_{x,y},b)[\mathbb G]
\right).
\]
The population delta-method variance is bounded below by \(\eta\):
\[
V_{r_0,x,y}(\mathcal M;p)\ge\eta.
\]

c4156d581a0d7630c6cdc2ebef7f4982e71b3e9c.title: Balancing fiber \(\Lambda_x(\mathcal D)\)
c4156d581a0d7630c6cdc2ebef7f4982e71b3e9c.body:
Define the conditional proxy matrix \(B_x\) by
\[
B_x(w,e)=P_O(W=w\mid E=e,X=x).
\]
The balancing fiber is
\[
\Lambda_x(\mathcal D)
=
\{\lambda\in\mathbb R^{\lvert\mathcal E\rvert}:B_x\lambda=b\}.
\]

681c18a509ab809e596f8872cc32040910230a7f.title: Projection set \(\widehat C_{x,y,1-\alpha}\)
681c18a509ab809e596f8872cc32040910230a7f.body:
Define the empirical source moment matrix, empirical source outcome-moment vector, and empirical target proxy vector by
\[
\widehat H_x(e,w)
=
\frac{1}{n_s}\sum_{i=1}^{n_s}
\mathbf 1\{E_i^s=e,W_i^s=w,X_i^s=x\},
\]
\[
\widehat z_{x,y}(e)
=
\frac{1}{n_s}\sum_{i=1}^{n_s}
\mathbf 1\{E_i^s=e,X_i^s=x,Y_i^s=y\},
\]
\[
\widehat b(w)
=
\frac{1}{n_t}\sum_{j=1}^{n_t}
\mathbf 1\{W_j^t=w\}.
\]
Let
\[
L=m\lvert\mathcal E\rvert+\lvert\mathcal E\rvert+m,
\qquad
r_s=\sqrt{\frac{\log(2L/\alpha)}{2n_s}},
\qquad
r_t=\sqrt{\frac{\log(2L/\alpha)}{2n_t}}.
\]
Define
\[
\widehat C_{x,y,1-\alpha}
=
\left\{
\vartheta\in[0,1]:
\exists \kappa\in\mathbb R^{\lvert\mathcal E\rvert}
\text{ such that }
\lVert \widehat H_x\kappa-\widehat b\rVert_{\infty}
\le
r_s\lVert\kappa\rVert_1+r_t
\text{ and }
\left|\widehat z_{x,y}^{\top}\kappa-\vartheta\right|
\le
r_s\lVert\kappa\rVert_1
\right\}.
\]

9d0f67d0ce3ddd9729e15744155c1d7197422f72.title: Array class \(\mathcal A_p\)
9d0f67d0ce3ddd9729e15744155c1d7197422f72.body:
Fix \(p\in(0,1)\) and a deterministic allocation sequence \((n_s(n),n_t(n))_{n\ge2}\) satisfying \(\cref{obj:ass:triangular-allocation}\). Relative to this sequence, and under \(\cref{obj:ass:triangular-source-iid-sampling,obj:ass:triangular-target-iid-sampling,obj:ass:array-target-span}\), define the minimum balancing-weight norm in row \(n\) by
\[
d_{x,n}
=
\inf\left\{
\lVert\lambda\rVert_2:
\lambda\in\mathbb R^{\lvert\mathcal E\rvert},
\ B_{x,n}\lambda=b_n
\right\}.
\]
Define
\[
\mathcal A_p
=
\left\{
\mathbb M=(\mathcal M_n)_{n\ge2}:
\begin{array}{l}
\text{for every } n\ge2,\ 
\mathbb P_{\mathcal M_n}^{\,n_s(n),n_t(n)}
=
P_{O,n}^{\otimes n_s(n)}\otimes b_n^{\otimes n_t(n)}
\text{ on } \Omega_n=\Omega(n_s(n),n_t(n)),\\
\text{and } b_n\in\operatorname{col}(B_{x,n})
\end{array}
\right\}.
\]
The class allows row-wise changes in \(\operatorname{rank}(B_{x,n})\), singular joint multinomial covariance, and divergent balancing-weight norm \(d_{x,n}\).

b92a2780da2b0e5c6f1a14e5428b5b51ffda5943.title: Row-wise Wald estimator \(\widehat\theta^{\,W}_{x,y,n}\)
b92a2780da2b0e5c6f1a14e5428b5b51ffda5943.body:
Define the row-wise empirical source moment matrix \(\widehat H_{x,n}\) by
\[
\widehat H_{x,n}(e,w)
=
\frac{1}{n_s(n)}
\sum_{i=1}^{n_s(n)}
\mathbf 1\{E_i^s=e,\ W_i^s=w,\ X_i^s=x\}.
\]
Define the row-wise empirical source outcome-moment vector \(\widehat z_{x,y,n}\) by
\[
\widehat z_{x,y,n}(e)
=
\frac{1}{n_s(n)}
\sum_{i=1}^{n_s(n)}
\mathbf 1\{E_i^s=e,\ X_i^s=x,\ Y_i^s=y\}.
\]
Define the row-wise empirical target proxy vector \(\widehat b_n\) by
\[
\widehat b_n(w)
=
\frac{1}{n_t(n)}
\sum_{j=1}^{n_t(n)}
\mathbf 1\{W_j^t=w\}.
\]
The truncated-SVD Wald estimator is
\[
\widehat\theta^{\,W}_{x,y,n}
=
\phi_{r_0}(\widehat H_{x,n},\widehat z_{x,y,n},\widehat b_n).
\]

3ef21303fad3a98d2f0125b66221dc967b9a1441.title: Observable factorization identities
3ef21303fad3a98d2f0125b66221dc967b9a1441.body:
Let \(\mathcal M\) be a latent-shift SCM on finite state spaces \(\mathcal E,\mathcal U,\mathcal W,\mathcal X,\mathcal Y\), and suppose that \(\mathcal M\in\mathfrak M_{+}\) in the sense of \cref{obj:def:positive-latent-shift-class}. For \(x\in\mathcal X\), define the latent posterior matrix \(R_x\in\mathbb R^{\mathcal U\times\mathcal E}\) by
\[
R_x(u,e)=\frac{a_x(u)S(u,e)}{\rho_x(e)} .
\]
For \(x\in\mathcal X\) and \(y\in\mathcal Y\), define the latent-proxy averaged outcome vector \(g_{x,y}\in\mathbb R^{\mathcal U}\) by
\[
g_{x,y}(u)=\sum_{w\in\mathcal W}M(w,u)f_{x,y}(u,w).
\]
Then, for every \(x\in\mathcal X\) and \(y\in\mathcal Y\),
\[
B_x = M R_x,\qquad
b = Mq,\qquad
c_{x,y}=g_{x,y}^{\top}R_x,\qquad
\theta_{x,y}=g_{x,y}^{\top}q .
\]
Moreover, for every \(\lambda\in\Lambda_x(\mathcal D)\), with \(\Lambda_x(\mathcal D)\) specified by \cref{obj:def:balancing-fiber}, the unconditional weight \(\kappa\) induced by \(\lambda\) as in \cref{obj:def:unconditional-weight-map} satisfies
\[
H_x\kappa=b
\qquad\text{and}\qquad
z_{x,y}^{\top}\kappa=\theta_{x,y}.
\]
Finally, there exists a vector \(h:\mathcal W\to\mathbb R\) such that
\[
H_x^{\top}h=z_{x,y}.
\]

d31567acdcc35256aaef70da142011db53a45628.title: Uniform Wald adaptation fails
d31567acdcc35256aaef70da142011db53a45628.body:
Fix a source allocation limit \(p\in(0,1)\), an error level \(\alpha\in(0,1)\), and deterministic allocation sequences \(n_s(n)\) and \(n_t(n)\) satisfying \cref{obj:ass:triangular-allocation}. For each \(n\), write \(\Omega_n=\Omega(n_s(n),n_t(n))\). For any row array \(\mathbb M=(\mathcal M_n)_{n\ge 0}\), define the row-\(n\) target interventional probability by
\[
\theta_{x,y,n}(\mathbb M)
=
\theta_{x,y}(\mathcal M_n)
=
\sum_{u,w} q_n(u)M_n(w\mid u)f_{n,x,y}(u,w).
\]
Then there exist a fixed latent-shift SCM \(\mathcal M^{(0)}\) with \(\mathcal E=\mathcal U=\mathcal W=\mathcal Y=\{0,1\}\) and singleton \(\mathcal X=\{0\}\), and a two-sample triangular array \(\mathbb M^{(1)}=(\mathcal M^{(1)}_n)_{n\ge 0}\) on the same state spaces and allocation sequences, such that:
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Regular baseline.)} \(\mathcal M^{(0)}\in\mathcal R_{1,1/4,1/16}\) for treatment \(x=0\), outcome \(y=1\), and source allocation limit \(p\).
\item \textbf{(Array class.)} \(\mathbb M^{(1)}\in\mathcal A_p\) for treatment \(x=0\) and the allocation sequences \(n_s,n_t\).
\item \textbf{(Separated targets.)} The baseline and row targets satisfy
\[
\theta_{0,1}(\mathcal M^{(0)})=\frac12,
\qquad
\theta_{0,1,n}(\mathbb M^{(1)})=\frac58
\quad\text{for every } n\ge 2 .
\]
\item \textbf{(Contiguous row laws.)} The row laws induced by \(\mathbb M^{(1)}\) and by repeating \(\mathcal M^{(0)}\) along the same allocation sequence satisfy
\[
d_{\mathrm{TV}}\!\left(
\mathbb P_{\mathcal M^{(1)}_n}^{\,n_s(n),n_t(n)},
\mathbb P_{\mathcal M^{(0)}}^{\,n_s(n),n_t(n)}
\right)\longrightarrow 0 .
\]
\end{itemize}
Consequently, for every confidence-set sequence \((\mathcal C_n)_{n\ge 0}\), with each \(\mathcal C_n(\omega)\) nonempty and contained in \([0,1]\), satisfying
\[
1-\alpha
\le
\liminf_{n\to\infty}
\inf_{\mathbb M\in\mathcal A_p}
\mathbb P_{\mathcal M_n}^{\,n_s(n),n_t(n)}
\!\left\{
\theta_{0,1,n}(\mathbb M)\in\mathcal C_n
\right\},
\]
and for every Wald-localization slack \(\varepsilon\in(0,1/8)\),
\[
1-\alpha
\le
\liminf_{n\to\infty}
\mathbb P_{\mathcal M^{(0)}}^{\,n_s(n),n_t(n)}
\!\left\{
I^W_{n,1-\alpha}(\omega)\ne\varnothing,\ 
\frac18-\varepsilon
\le
d_H\!\left(\mathcal C_n(\omega),I^W_{n,1-\alpha}(\omega)\right)
\right\},
\]
where \(I^W_{n,1-\alpha}(\omega)\) is the rank-\(1\) studentized truncated-SVD Wald interval for treatment \(0\), outcome \(1\), source allocation limit \(p\), allocation sequences \(n_s,n_t\), and baseline \(\mathcal M^{(0)}\), with the displayed event interpreted as all of \(\Omega_n\) for the finitely many rows \(n<2\).

c10afad66b4e73504c556237ddc4dc3b0aea436b.title: Row target span
c10afad66b4e73504c556237ddc4dc3b0aea436b.body:
For each \(n\), let \(B_{x,n}\) be the row-\(n\) conditional proxy matrix with entries
\[
B_{x,n}(w,e)=P_{O,n}(W=w\mid E=e,X=x),
\qquad w\in\mathcal W,\ e\in\mathcal E.
\]
The row-\(n\) target proxy law satisfies
\[
b_n\in\operatorname{col}(B_{x,n}).
\]

ddda8e62f2568387ead0b630abcd1054846816bf.title: Fixed moment rank
ddda8e62f2568387ead0b630abcd1054846816bf.body:
Let \(H_x\) be the unconditional source moment matrix with entries
\[
H_x(w,e)=P_O(E=e,W=w,X=x),
\qquad w\in\mathcal W,\ e\in\mathcal E.
\]
The fixed source moment matrix satisfies
\[
\operatorname{rank}(H_x)=r_0.
\]

bff5ad3df19426b82c8e837bbe9fcda861d611ab.title: Positive Wald variance
bff5ad3df19426b82c8e837bbe9fcda861d611ab.body:
Let \(V_{r_0,x,y}(\mathcal M;p)\) be the population delta-method variance of the retained-rank Wald functional,
\[
V_{r_0,x,y}(\mathcal M;p)
=
D\phi_{r_0}(H_x,z_{x,y},b)\,
\Gamma_{x,y}(\mathcal M;p)\,
D\phi_{r_0}(H_x,z_{x,y},b)^{\top},
\]
where \(\Gamma_{x,y}(\mathcal M;p)\) is the population covariance matrix of the fixed-allocation source and target-proxy moment limit. This variance satisfies
\[
V_{r_0,x,y}(\mathcal M;p)\ge\eta.
\]

ea8a91daaafd6c6a68c0298a8b3127e1be26fc07.title: Balancing fiber \(\Lambda_x(\mathcal D)\)
ea8a91daaafd6c6a68c0298a8b3127e1be26fc07.body:
Define the conditional proxy matrix \(B_x\) by
\[
B_x(w,e)=P_O(W=w\mid E=e,X=x),
\qquad w\in\mathcal W,\ e\in\mathcal E.
\]
The balancing fiber is
\[
\Lambda_x(\mathcal D)
=
\{\lambda\in\mathbb R^{\lvert\mathcal E\rvert}:B_x\lambda=b\}.
\]

75b789f5c5354dcaa494d7e100688f1500def5ba.body:

d680ab48658dc36cd4ab1cbcef33fe7385db1a85.title: Observable factorization
d680ab48658dc36cd4ab1cbcef33fe7385db1a85.body:
Let \(\mathcal M\) be a normalized finite latent-shift SCM on finite state spaces \(\mathcal E,\mathcal U,\mathcal W,\mathcal X,\mathcal Y\), with nonempty \(\mathcal E\) and \(\mathcal X\), \(2\le |\mathcal U|\), \(|\mathcal U|\le |\mathcal W|\), and \(2\le |\mathcal Y|\). \[
\rho_x(e)=\sum_{w\in\mathcal W}\sum_{y\in\mathcal Y}P_O(e,w,x,y).

R_x(u,e)=\frac{a_x(u)S(u,e)}{\rho_x(e)}

B_x = M R_x,

c_{x,y}=R_x^{\top}g_{x,y},
\qquad
\theta_{x,y}=g_{x,y}^{\top}q .

H_x\kappa=b
\qquad\text{and}\qquad

\]

1dda46a825ec3d6c3503868df0c07f1d91f6e465.title: Source iid sampling
1dda46a825ec3d6c3503868df0c07f1d91f6e465.body: Let \(P_O\) denote the observed-source marginal law induced by the latent-shift SCM. The source observations \(O_1^s,\ldots,O_{n_s}^s\) are independent and identically distributed according to \(P_O\).

811352eeb7a5248add80325dcfe57976d6b56134.title: Target-proxy iid sampling
811352eeb7a5248add80325dcfe57976d6b56134.body: Let \(b\) denote the target proxy marginal law. The target-proxy observations \(W_1^t,\ldots,W_{n_t}^t\) are independent and identically distributed according to \(b\).

da32bd05ca722555781e636635b4f366258eb044.title: Triangular source sampling
da32bd05ca722555781e636635b4f366258eb044.body:
For every \(n\ge 2\), let
\[
\Omega_n=\Omega(n_s(n),n_t(n))
\]
be the row-\(n\) finite two-sample product space. The source observations
\[
(O^s_{1,n},\ldots,O^s_{n_s(n),n})
\]
are the source coordinate block under the finite row law
\[
\mathbb P_{\mathcal M_n}^{\,n_s(n),n_t(n)}
=
P_{O,n}^{\otimes n_s(n)}\otimes b_n^{\otimes n_t(n)}
\]
on \(\Omega_n\).

26f616917c3fed119135c89ebbb7f77238018eb1.title: Wald functional \(\phi_{r_0}\)
26f616917c3fed119135c89ebbb7f77238018eb1.body:
For \(H\in\mathbb R^{m\times\lvert\mathcal E\rvert}\), write its singular-value decomposition with nonincreasing singular values as
\[
H=\sum_{k=1}^{\bar q}\sigma_k(H)u_kv_k^{\top},
\qquad
\bar q=\min(m,\lvert\mathcal E\rvert).
\]
At a tied singular-value cutoff, a fixed selector chooses the retained \(r_0\) singular directions among the directions in the cutoff eigenspace. Define the selector-based Gram-spectral rank-\(r_0\) truncation by
\[
H^{\star}_{r_0}
=
\sum_{k\in I_{r_0}(H)}\sigma_k(H)u_kv_k^{\top},
\]
where \(I_{r_0}(H)\) is the selected set of \(r_0\) retained singular directions. Put
\[
H_{r_0}=H^{\star}_{r_0}.
\]
For \(z\in\mathbb R^{\lvert\mathcal E\rvert}\) and \(b\in\mathbb R^m\), define
\[
\phi_{r_0}(H,z,b)=z^{\top}H_{r_0}^{\dagger}b.
\]
The selector fixes a single value of \(\phi_{r_0}\) at tied cutoffs. If
\[
\sigma_{r_0}(H)>\sigma_{r_0+1}(H),
\]
then the retained subspace is unique, and \(H_{r_0}\) and \(\phi_{r_0}(H,z,b)\) are independent of the fixed within-tie selector.

b2798fe1eca54758ddf6e17b5988bcd944029806.title: Wald estimator \(\widehat\theta^{\,W}_{x,y,n}\)
b2798fe1eca54758ddf6e17b5988bcd944029806.body:
Define the truncated-SVD Wald estimator by
\[
\widehat\theta^{\,W}_{x,y,n}
=
\phi_{r_0}(\widehat H_{x,n},\widehat z_{x,y,n},\widehat b_n).
\]
The row-\(n\) empirical source moment matrix is
\[
\widehat H_{x,n}(w,e)
=
\frac{1}{n_s(n)}
\sum_{i=1}^{n_s(n)}
\mathbf 1\{E_i^s=e,\ W_i^s=w,\ X_i^s=x\}.
\]
The row-\(n\) empirical source outcome-moment vector is
\[
\widehat z_{x,y,n}(e)
=
\frac{1}{n_s(n)}
\sum_{i=1}^{n_s(n)}
\mathbf 1\{E_i^s=e,\ X_i^s=x,\ Y_i^s=y\}.
\]
The row-\(n\) empirical target proxy vector is
\[
\widehat b_n(w)
=
\frac{1}{n_t(n)}
\sum_{j=1}^{n_t(n)}
\mathbf 1\{W_j^t=w\}.
\]

37aa47f357e31f8f268d16727bfaa3c337a77991.title: Wald variance \(\widehat V_n\)
37aa47f357e31f8f268d16727bfaa3c337a77991.body:
Put
\[
\widehat T_n=(\widehat H_{x,n},\widehat z_{x,y,n},\widehat b_n),
\]
where \(\widehat H_{x,n}\in\mathbb R^{m\times\lvert\mathcal E\rvert}\) is indexed as \(\widehat H_{x,n}(w,e)\). Let \(\widehat\Gamma_n\) be the plug-in covariance matrix of \(\sqrt n\,\widehat T_n\), formed from the joint source multinomial covariance and the target multinomial covariance with allocation factors \(p^{-1}\) and \((1-p)^{-1}\). Define the totalized plug-in variance by
\[
\widehat V_n=
\begin{cases}
D\phi_{r_0}(\widehat T_n)\,\widehat\Gamma_n\,D\phi_{r_0}(\widehat T_n)^{\top},
&\sigma_{r_0}(\widehat H_{x,n})>\sigma_{r_0+1}(\widehat H_{x,n}),\\
0,&\sigma_{r_0}(\widehat H_{x,n})\le\sigma_{r_0+1}(\widehat H_{x,n}),
\end{cases}
\]
where \(D\phi_{r_0}\) is the ordinary derivative of the selector-independent functional on the strict-cutoff-gap region, and where
\[
\sigma_{\bar q+1}=0,
\qquad
\bar q=\min(m,\lvert\mathcal E\rvert).
\]
The second line is the fixed nonnegative fallback.

0635935bb6d42d9a45c0e3806f5071535f8896b8.title: Truncated-SVD Wald interval \(I^W_{n,1-\alpha}\)
0635935bb6d42d9a45c0e3806f5071535f8896b8.body:
Let \(\Phi\) denote the standard-normal distribution function, and set
\[
z_{1-\alpha/2}=\Phi^{-1}(1-\alpha/2).
\]
The truncated-SVD Wald interval is
\[
I^W_{n,1-\alpha}
=
\left[
\widehat\theta^{\,W}_{x,y,n}
\pm
z_{1-\alpha/2}\sqrt{\widehat V_n/n}
\right]\cap[0,1].
\]

650d456579a27dac0fff5e0218cdb66a988ae512.title: Finite-sample projection coverage
650d456579a27dac0fff5e0218cdb66a988ae512.body:
Let \(\mathcal M\) be a latent-shift SCM on finite state spaces \(\mathcal E,\mathcal U,\mathcal W,\mathcal X,\mathcal Y\), let \(P_O\) be an observed source law, and let \(b\) be a target proxy law. Fix \(x\in\mathcal X\) and \(y\in\mathcal Y\). Suppose that
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Positive latent shift.)} \(\mathcal M\in\mathfrak M_{+}\) in the sense of \cref{obj:def:positive-latent-shift-class}.
\item \textbf{(Compatibility.)} \(\mathcal M\in\mathfrak F(\mathcal D)\), with \(\mathcal D=(P_O,b)\), in the sense of \cref{obj:def:compatible-fiber}.
\item \textbf{(Balancing feasibility.)} The affine balancing set \(\Lambda_x(\mathcal D)\) from \cref{obj:def:balancing-fiber} is nonempty; equivalently, there exists \(\lambda:\mathcal E\to\mathbb R\) such that \(B_x\lambda=b\).
\item \textbf{(Sample sizes and level.)} The sample sizes satisfy \(n_s>0\) and \(n_t>0\), and the nominal error level satisfies \(0<\alpha<1\).
\end{itemize}
Let
\[
\mathbb P_{\mathcal M}^{\,n_s,n_t}
=
P_O^{\otimes n_s}\otimes b^{\otimes n_t}
\]
on the finite two-sample product space, with independent source observations \(O_i^s=(E_i^s,W_i^s,X_i^s,Y_i^s)\) and independent target proxy observations \(W_j^t\). Form \(\widehat H_x\), \(\widehat z_{x,y}\), and \(\widehat b\) by
\[
\widehat H_x(w,e)
=
\frac{1}{n_s}\sum_{i=1}^{n_s}
\mathbf 1\{E_i^s=e,\ W_i^s=w,\ X_i^s=x\},
\qquad
\widehat z_{x,y}(e)
=
\frac{1}{n_s}\sum_{i=1}^{n_s}
\mathbf 1\{E_i^s=e,\ X_i^s=x,\ Y_i^s=y\},
\]
and
\[
\widehat b(w)
=
\frac{1}{n_t}\sum_{j=1}^{n_t}\mathbf 1\{W_j^t=w\}.
\]
Then
\[
1-\alpha
\le
\mathbb P_{\mathcal M}^{\,n_s,n_t}
\left\{
\sum_{u\in\mathcal U}\sum_{w\in\mathcal W}
q(u)M(w,u)f_{x,y}(u,w)
\in
\widehat C_{x,y,1-\alpha}
\right\},
\]
where \(\widehat C_{x,y,1-\alpha}\) is the concentration-calibrated projection set of \cref{obj:def:concentration-projection-set} formed from \(\widehat H_x\), \(\widehat z_{x,y}\), \(\widehat b\), \(n_s\), \(n_t\), and \(\alpha\).

a87bafca3676ecbe81e740a8b442fdc5dfbffc4f.title: Failure separators $\mathcal H_x(\mathcal D)$
a87bafca3676ecbe81e740a8b442fdc5dfbffc4f.body:
Let
\[
m=\lvert\mathcal W\rvert .
\]
The observed separator set for treatment value \(x\) is
\[
\mathcal H_x(\mathcal D)
=
\{h\in\mathbb R^m: h^{\top}B_x=0,\ h^{\top}b\ne 0\}.
\]

905019f016250d2ce067573ca68cae10280864ab.title: Studentized array class $\mathcal A_p$
905019f016250d2ce067573ca68cae10280864ab.body:
For source and target sample sizes \(n_s\) and \(n_t\), define the two-sample product-space family by
\[
\Omega(n_s,n_t)
=
(\mathcal E\times\mathcal W\times\mathcal X\times\mathcal Y)^{n_s}
\times
\mathcal W^{n_t}.
\]
Fix \(p\in(0,1)\) and a deterministic allocation sequence \((n_s(n),n_t(n))_{n\ge2}\) satisfying \cref{obj:ass:triangular-allocation}. Relative to this sequence, and under \cref{obj:ass:triangular-source-iid-sampling,obj:ass:triangular-target-iid-sampling,obj:ass:array-target-span}, define
\[
\mathcal A_p
=
\left\{
\mathbb M=(\mathcal M_n)_{n\ge2}:
\begin{array}{l}
\text{for every } n\ge2,\ 
\mathbb P_{\mathcal M_n}^{\,n_s(n),n_t(n)}
=
P_{O,n}^{\otimes n_s(n)}\otimes b_n^{\otimes n_t(n)}
\text{ on } \Omega_n=\Omega(n_s(n),n_t(n)),\\
\text{and } b_n\in\operatorname{col}(B_{x,n})
\end{array}
\right\}.
\]
For each row \(n\), the minimum balancing-weight norm is
\[
d_{x,n}
=
\inf\left\{
\lVert\lambda\rVert_2:
\lambda\in\mathbb R^{\lvert\mathcal E\rvert}
\text{ and }
B_{x,n}\lambda=b_n
\right\}.
\]
The class allows row-wise changes in \(\operatorname{rank}(B_{x,n})\), singular joint multinomial covariance, and divergent balancing-weight norm \(d_{x,n}\).

4243cbe9e30d372b2acf0707ee6718dd8f1652d5.title: Full-rank proxy channel
4243cbe9e30d372b2acf0707ee6718dd8f1652d5.body:
Let
\[
r=\lvert\mathcal U\rvert
\]
be the latent cardinality. The proxy channel \(M\) has full column rank:
\[
\operatorname{rank}(M)=r.
\]

5c71e65e56dfc469861f03519c8b02c7d2f1b181.title: Triangular source sampling
5c71e65e56dfc469861f03519c8b02c7d2f1b181.body:
For every \(n\ge 2\), let \(P_{O,n}\) be the observed-source law induced by the row-\(n\) SCM \(\mathcal M_n\), and let \(b_n\) be the target-proxy law induced by \(\mathcal M_n\). Let
\[
\Omega_n=\Omega(n_s(n),n_t(n))
\]
be the row-\(n\) finite two-sample product space. The source observations
\[
(O^s_{1,n},\ldots,O^s_{n_s(n),n})
\]
are the source coordinate block under the finite row law
\[
\mathbb P_{\mathcal M_n}^{\,n_s(n),n_t(n)}
=
P_{O,n}^{\otimes n_s(n)}\otimes b_n^{\otimes n_t(n)}
\]
on \(\Omega_n\).

988ad9b3d0616f6ff69796c5812df64e29e234e9.title: Positive Wald variance
988ad9b3d0616f6ff69796c5812df64e29e234e9.body:
For each environment \(e\), let
\[
z_{x,y}(e)=P_O(E=e,X=x,Y=y).
\]
Let \(\phi_{r_0}\) be the retained-rank Wald functional. Let \(V_{r_0,x,y}(\mathcal M;p)\) be the population delta-method variance of this functional,
\[
V_{r_0,x,y}(\mathcal M;p)
=
D\phi_{r_0}(H_x,z_{x,y},b)\,
\Gamma_{x,y}(\mathcal M;p)\,
D\phi_{r_0}(H_x,z_{x,y},b)^{\top},
\]
where \(\Gamma_{x,y}(\mathcal M;p)\) is the population covariance matrix of the fixed-allocation source and target-proxy moment limit. This variance satisfies
\[
V_{r_0,x,y}(\mathcal M;p)\ge\eta.
\]

1fed26954c77b184650ec4388e2399d1ee460353.title: Positive latent-shift class \(\mathfrak M_{+}\)
1fed26954c77b184650ec4388e2399d1ee460353.body:
\[
\mathfrak M_{+}
=
\{\mathcal M=(\pi,S,M,a,f,q):
\mathcal M \text{ satisfies } \cref{obj:ass:latent-shift-factorization,obj:ass:target-mechanism-invariance,obj:ass:strict-primitive-positivity,obj:ass:proxy-channel-injectivity}\}.
\]
Equivalently, \(\mathfrak M_{+}\) is the class of strictly positive latent-shift SCMs with invariant target mechanism and full-column-rank proxy channel.

2d7f890e263d28728d4cdbdde19bc4713a7df0c1.title: Wald adaptation obstruction
2d7f890e263d28728d4cdbdde19bc4713a7df0c1.body:
Fix a source allocation limit \(p\in(0,1)\), an error level \(\alpha\in(0,1)\), and deterministic allocation sequences \(n_s,n_t:\mathbb N\to\mathbb N\) satisfying \cref{obj:ass:triangular-allocation}. For each row \(n\), let
\[
\Omega_n=\Omega(n_s(n),n_t(n)).
\]
For a two-sample triangular array \(\mathbb M=(\mathcal M_n)_{n\ge 0}\), write
\[
\theta_{x,y,n}(\mathbb M)
=
\theta_{x,y}(\mathcal M_n)
=
\sum_{u,w} q_n(u)M_n(w\mid u)f_{n,x,y}(u,w).
\]
Then there exist a fixed latent-shift SCM \(\mathcal M^{(0)}\) with
\(\mathcal E=\mathcal U=\mathcal W=\mathcal Y=\{0,1\}\) and singleton
\(\mathcal X=\{0\}\), and a two-sample triangular array
\(\mathbb M^{(1)}=(\mathcal M^{(1)}_n)_{n\ge 0}\) on the same state spaces and allocation sequences, such that:
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Regular baseline.)} \(\mathcal M^{(0)}\in\mathcal R_{1,1/4,1/16}\) for treatment \(x=0\), outcome \(y=1\), and source allocation limit \(p\).
\item \textbf{(Array class.)} \(\mathbb M^{(1)}\) belongs to the fixed-allocation studentized array class \(\mathcal A_p\) for treatment \(x=0\) and allocation sequences \(n_s,n_t\), the class of positive two-sample arrays satisfying the specified allocation, row-law, sampling, and target-span conditions.
\item \textbf{(Separated targets.)} The baseline and row targets satisfy
\[
\theta_{0,1}(\mathcal M^{(0)})=\frac12,
\qquad
\theta_{0,1,n}(\mathbb M^{(1)})=\frac58
\quad\text{for every } n\ge 2 .
\]
\item \textbf{(Contiguous row laws.)} The row laws induced by \(\mathbb M^{(1)}\) and by repeating \(\mathcal M^{(0)}\) along the same allocation sequence satisfy
\[
d_{\mathrm{TV}}\!\left(
\mathbb P_{\mathcal M^{(1)}_n}^{\,n_s(n),n_t(n)},
\mathbb P_{\mathcal M^{(0)}}^{\,n_s(n),n_t(n)}
\right)\longrightarrow 0 .
\]
\end{itemize}
Consequently, for every confidence-set sequence \((\mathcal C_n)_{n\ge 0}\), with each \(\mathcal C_n(\omega)\) nonempty and contained in \([0,1]\), if
\[
1-\alpha
\le
\liminf_{n\to\infty}
\inf_{\mathbb M\in\mathcal A_p}
\mathbb P_{\mathcal M_n}^{\,n_s(n),n_t(n)}
\!\left\{
\theta_{0,1,n}(\mathbb M)\in\mathcal C_n
\right\},
\]
then, for every Wald-localization slack \(\varepsilon\in(0,1/8)\),
\[
1-\alpha
\le
\liminf_{n\to\infty}
\mathbb P_{\mathcal M^{(0)}}^{\,n_s(n),n_t(n)}
\!\left\{
I^W_{n,1-\alpha}(\omega)\ne\varnothing,\ 
\frac18-\varepsilon
\le
d_H\!\left(\mathcal C_n(\omega),I^W_{n,1-\alpha}(\omega)\right)
\right\},
\]
where \(I^W_{n,1-\alpha}(\omega)\) is the rank-\(1\) studentized truncated-SVD Wald interval for treatment \(0\), outcome \(1\), source allocation limit \(p\), allocation sequences \(n_s,n_t\), and baseline \(\mathcal M^{(0)}\), and the displayed event is interpreted as all of \(\Omega_n\) for rows \(n<2\).

741ddc38ba648c7948946bfb8d3d7624c34bd0b2.title: Positive Wald variance
741ddc38ba648c7948946bfb8d3d7624c34bd0b2.body:
For each environment \(e\), the unconditional source outcome-moment vector is
\[
z_{x,y}(e)=P_O(E=e,X=x,Y=y).
\]
For a moment triple \((H,z,b)\), let \(H_{r_0}=H^{\star}_{r_0}\) denote the selector-based Gram-spectral rank-\(r_0\) truncation of \(H\), and define the retained-rank Wald functional by
\[
\phi_{r_0}(H,z,b)=z^{\top}H_{r_0}^{\dagger}b.
\]
Let \(V_{r_0,x,y}(\mathcal M;p)\) be the population delta-method variance of \(\phi_{r_0}\) at \((H_x,z_{x,y},b)\),
\[
V_{r_0,x,y}(\mathcal M;p)
=
D\phi_{r_0}(H_x,z_{x,y},b)\,
\Gamma_{x,y}(\mathcal M;p)\,
D\phi_{r_0}(H_x,z_{x,y},b)^{\top},
\]
where \(\Gamma_{x,y}(\mathcal M;p)\) is the population covariance matrix of the fixed-allocation source and target-proxy moment limit. The variance satisfies
\[
V_{r_0,x,y}(\mathcal M;p)\ge \eta.
\]

340c6aff6cbe7dba1bf053fd367a9920a0f2bac3.title: Observable factorization
340c6aff6cbe7dba1bf053fd367a9920a0f2bac3.body:
Let \(\mathcal M\) be a latent-shift SCM on finite state spaces \(\mathcal E,\mathcal U,\mathcal W,\mathcal X,\mathcal Y\), and suppose that \(\mathcal M\in\mathfrak M_{+}\) in the sense of \cref{obj:def:positive-latent-shift-class}. For \(x\in\mathcal X\), define the source treatment probability and latent posterior matrix by
\[
\rho_x(e)=\sum_{u\in\mathcal U} a_x(u)S(u,e),
\qquad
R_x(u,e)=\frac{a_x(u)S(u,e)}{\rho_x(e)} .
\]
For \(x\in\mathcal X\) and \(y\in\mathcal Y\), define the latent-proxy averaged outcome vector by
\[
g_{x,y}(u)=\sum_{w\in\mathcal W} M(w,u)f_{x,y}(u,w).
\]
Then, for every \(x\in\mathcal X\) and \(y\in\mathcal Y\),
\[
B_x = M R_x,\qquad
b = Mq,\qquad
c_{x,y}=g_{x,y}^{\top}R_x,\qquad
\theta_{x,y}=g_{x,y}^{\top}q .
\]
Moreover, for every \(\lambda\in\Lambda_x(\mathcal D)\), where \(\Lambda_x(\mathcal D)\) is the balancing fiber in \cref{obj:def:balancing-fiber}, the unconditional weight \(\kappa\) induced by \(\lambda\) as in \cref{obj:def:unconditional-weight-map} satisfies
\[
H_x\kappa=b
\qquad\text{and}\qquad
z_{x,y}^{\top}\kappa=\theta_{x,y}.
\]
Finally, there exists a vector \(h:\mathcal W\to\mathbb R\) such that
\[
H_x^{\top}h=z_{x,y}.
\]

f9b70e4bf76449e0e79a09e923f170a5627274d6.title: Row-wise target span
f9b70e4bf76449e0e79a09e923f170a5627274d6.body:
For each \(n\), let \(B_{x,n}\) denote the row-\(n\) conditional proxy matrix with entries
\[
B_{x,n}(e,w)=P_{O,n}(W=w\mid E=e,X=x),
\qquad e\in\mathcal E,\ w\in\mathcal W .
\]
The row-\(n\) target proxy law \(b_n\) satisfies
\[
b_n\in\operatorname{col}(B_{x,n}).
\]

d3b43281b05815bf5ea2b4fb754c4886dbf1f153.title: Positive Wald variance
d3b43281b05815bf5ea2b4fb754c4886dbf1f153.body:
Let \(V_{r_0,x,y}(\mathcal M;p)\) denote the population delta-method variance of the retained-rank Wald functional \(\phi_{r_0}\) at the population moment tuple \((H_x,z_{x,y},b)\), with source allocation limit \(p\) and target-proxy allocation limit \(1-p\). It satisfies
\[
V_{r_0,x,y}(\mathcal M;p)\ge\eta .
\]

ae720988bc68bcd3318f0a10c49df84c947cb9ec.title: Studentized array class \(\mathcal A_p\)
ae720988bc68bcd3318f0a10c49df84c947cb9ec.body:
Fix \(p\in(0,1)\) and a deterministic allocation sequence \((n_s(n),n_t(n))_{n\ge2}\) satisfying \cref{obj:ass:triangular-allocation}. Relative to this sequence, and under \cref{obj:ass:triangular-source-iid-sampling,obj:ass:triangular-target-iid-sampling,obj:ass:array-target-span}, define
\[
d_{x,n}
=
\inf\left\{
\|\lambda\|_2:
\lambda\in\mathbb R^{|\mathcal E|},\ B_{x,n}\lambda=b_n
\right\}.
\]
The fixed-allocation changing-rank array class is
\[
\mathcal A_p
=
\left\{
\mathbb M=(\mathcal M_n)_{n\ge2}:
\begin{array}{l}
\text{for every } n\ge2,\ 
\mathbb P_{\mathcal M_n}^{\,n_s(n),n_t(n)}
=
P_{O,n}^{\otimes n_s(n)}\otimes b_n^{\otimes n_t(n)}
\text{ on } \Omega_n=\Omega(n_s(n),n_t(n)),\\
\text{and } b_n\in\operatorname{col}(B_{x,n})
\end{array}
\right\}.
\]
The class includes arrays with row-wise changes in \(\operatorname{rank}(B_{x,n})\), singular joint multinomial covariance, and divergent balancing-weight norm \(d_{x,n}\).

f32c9870c2275c34e727d29f09532e5066bb125a.body:

\[
\mathbb P_{\mathcal M}^{\,n_s,n_t}

\[

\le
\mathbb P_{\mathcal M}^{\,n_s,n_t}
\left\{
\sum_{u\in\mathcal U}\sum_{w\in\mathcal W}
q(u)M(w,u)f_{x,y}(u,w)
\in
\widehat C_{x,y,1-\alpha}
\right\},
\]
where \(\widehat C_{x,y,1-\alpha}\) is the concentration-calibrated projection set of \cref{obj:def:concentration-projection-set} formed from \(\widehat H_x\), \(\widehat z_{x,y}\), \(\widehat b\), \(n_s\), \(n_t\), and \(\alpha\).

1864cd1e907538792e226a2204bdbb4ef4a84895.title: Wald adaptation separation
1864cd1e907538792e226a2204bdbb4ef4a84895.body:
Fix a source allocation limit \(p\in(0,1)\), an error level \(\alpha\in(0,1)\), and deterministic allocation sequences \(n_s(n)\) and \(n_t(n)\) satisfying \cref{obj:ass:triangular-allocation}. For each \(n\ge2\), write \(\Omega_n=\Omega(n_s(n),n_t(n))\), and for any triangular array \(\mathbb M=(\mathcal M_n)_{n\ge2}\) define the row-\(n\) target interventional probability by
\[
\theta_{0,1,n}(\mathcal M_n)
=
\sum_{u,w} q_n(u)M_n(w\mid u)f_{0,1,n}(u,w).
\]
Then there exist a fixed latent-shift SCM \(\mathcal M^{(0)}\) with \(\mathcal E=\mathcal U=\mathcal W=\mathcal Y=\{0,1\}\) and singleton treatment space \(\mathcal X=\{0\}\), and a two-sample triangular array \(\mathbb M^{(1)}=(\mathcal M^{(1)}_n)_{n\ge2}\) on the same state spaces and allocation sequences, such that:
\begin{itemize}
\item \textbf{(Regular baseline.)} \(\mathcal M^{(0)}\in\mathcal R_{1,1/4,1/16}\) for treatment \(0\), outcome \(1\), and source allocation limit \(p\).
\item \textbf{(Array class.)} \(\mathbb M^{(1)}\in\mathcal A_p\) for treatment \(0\) and the allocation sequences \(n_s,n_t\).
\item \textbf{(Separated targets.)} The baseline and row targets satisfy
\[
\theta_{0,1}(\mathcal M^{(0)})=\frac12,
\qquad
\theta_{0,1,n}(\mathcal M^{(1)}_n)=\frac58
\quad\text{for every } n\ge2 .
\]
\item \textbf{(Contiguous row laws.)} The row laws induced by \(\mathbb M^{(1)}\) and by repeating \(\mathcal M^{(0)}\) along the same allocation sequence satisfy
\[
d_{\mathrm{TV}}\!\left(
\mathbb P_{\mathcal M^{(1)}_n}^{\,n_s(n),n_t(n)},
\mathbb P_{\mathcal M^{(0)}}^{\,n_s(n),n_t(n)}
\right)\longrightarrow 0 .
\]
\end{itemize}
Consequently, for every confidence-set sequence \((\mathcal C_n)_{n\ge2}\), with each reported set nonempty and contained in \([0,1]\), satisfying the uniform array coverage condition
\[
1-\alpha
\le
\liminf_{n\to\infty}
\inf_{\mathbb M\in\mathcal A_p}
\mathbb P_{\mathcal M_n}^{\,n_s(n),n_t(n)}
\!\left\{
\theta_{0,1,n}(\mathcal M_n)\in\mathcal C_n
\right\},
\]
and for every Wald-localization slack \(\varepsilon\in(0,1/8)\), the rank-one Wald interval \(I^W_{n,1-\alpha}(\omega)\) computed at \(\mathcal M^{(0)}\), treatment \(0\), outcome \(1\), source allocation limit \(p\), allocation sequences \(n_s,n_t\), and nominal level \(\alpha\) satisfies
\[
1-\alpha
\le
\liminf_{n\to\infty}
\mathbb P_{\mathcal M^{(0)}}^{\,n_s(n),n_t(n)}
\!\left\{
I^W_{n,1-\alpha}\ne\varnothing,\ 
\frac18-\varepsilon
\le
d_H\!\left(\mathcal C_n(\omega),I^W_{n,1-\alpha}(\omega)\right)
\right\}.
\]

a145c888def191a5872a87383f4905a632ad47a6.title: Source iid sampling
a145c888def191a5872a87383f4905a632ad47a6.body:
The observed source marginal law \(P_O\) induced by \(P_{\mathcal M}\) is defined by
\[
P_O(e,w,x,y)
=
\sum_{u\in\mathcal U}
P_{\mathcal M}(E=e,U=u,W=w,X=x,Y=y).
\]
The source observations \(O_1^s,\ldots,O_{n_s}^s\) are independent and identically distributed according to \(P_O\).

38c17e03ad5dee240e13aa3ba0e4e19a8d514cb8.title: Target-proxy iid sampling
38c17e03ad5dee240e13aa3ba0e4e19a8d514cb8.body:
The target proxy marginal vector \(b\) induced by \(Q_{\mathcal M}\) is defined by
\[
b(w)=Q_{\mathcal M}(W=w),
\qquad w\in\mathcal W.
\]
The target-proxy observations \(W_1^t,\ldots,W_{n_t}^t\) are independent and identically distributed according to \(b\).

9fd29441efd0c520bc205b84fe2abe1104b91380.title: Triangular source sampling
9fd29441efd0c520bc205b84fe2abe1104b91380.body:
For row \(n\), the observed source law \(P_{O,n}\) is defined by
\[
P_{O,n}(e,w,x,y)
=
\sum_{u\in\mathcal U}
P_{\mathcal M_n}(E=e,U=u,W=w,X=x,Y=y),
\]
and the target proxy law \(b_n\) is defined by
\[
b_n(w)=Q_{\mathcal M_n}(W=w),
\qquad w\in\mathcal W.
\]
For sample sizes \(n_s,n_t\), the finite two-sample product sample space is
\[
\Omega(n_s,n_t)
=
(\mathcal E\times\mathcal W\times\mathcal X\times\mathcal Y)^{n_s}
\times
\mathcal W^{n_t},
\]
with
\[
\Omega_n=\Omega(n_s(n),n_t(n)).
\]
For every \(n\ge 2\), the source observations \((O^s_{1,n},\ldots,O^s_{n_s(n),n})\) are the source coordinate block under the finite row law
\[
\mathbb P_{\mathcal M_n}^{\,n_s(n),n_t(n)}
=
P_{O,n}^{\otimes n_s(n)}\otimes b_n^{\otimes n_t(n)}
\]
on \(\Omega_n\).

e97df13d38ddd8c3e0de53c5af89ebaf3c771fb2.title: Projection set \(\widehat C_{x,y,1-\alpha}\)
e97df13d38ddd8c3e0de53c5af89ebaf3c771fb2.body:
The empirical source moment matrix \(\widehat H_x\) is defined by
\[
\widehat H_x(e,w)
=
\frac{1}{n_s}\sum_{i=1}^{n_s}
\mathbf 1\{E_i^s=e,\ W_i^s=w,\ X_i^s=x\}.
\]
The empirical source outcome-moment vector \(\widehat z_{x,y}\) is defined by
\[
\widehat z_{x,y}(e)
=
\frac{1}{n_s}\sum_{i=1}^{n_s}
\mathbf 1\{E_i^s=e,\ X_i^s=x,\ Y_i^s=y\}.
\]
The empirical target proxy frequency vector \(\widehat b\) is defined by
\[
\widehat b(w)
=
\frac{1}{n_t}\sum_{j=1}^{n_t}
\mathbf 1\{W_j^t=w\}.
\]
Let
\[
L=m\lvert\mathcal E\rvert+\lvert\mathcal E\rvert+m,
\qquad
r_s=\sqrt{\frac{\log(2L/\alpha)}{2n_s}},
\qquad
r_t=\sqrt{\frac{\log(2L/\alpha)}{2n_t}}.
\]
Define
\[
\widehat C_{x,y,1-\alpha}
=
\left\{
\vartheta\in[0,1]:
\exists \kappa\in\mathbb R^{\lvert\mathcal E\rvert}
\text{ such that }
\lVert \widehat H_x\kappa-\widehat b\rVert_{\infty}
\le
r_s\lVert\kappa\rVert_1+r_t
\text{ and }
\left|\widehat z_{x,y}^{\top}\kappa-\vartheta\right|
\le
r_s\lVert\kappa\rVert_1
\right\}.
\]

2072fa442456b7a87f3920550b9ea4c170f4f8ee.title: Wald estimator \(\widehat\theta^{\,W}_{x,y,n}\)
2072fa442456b7a87f3920550b9ea4c170f4f8ee.body:
The row-\(n\) empirical source moment matrix \(\widehat H_{x,n}\) is defined by
\[
\widehat H_{x,n}(e,w)
=
\frac{1}{n_s(n)}
\sum_{i=1}^{n_s(n)}
\mathbf 1\{E^s_{i,n}=e,\ W^s_{i,n}=w,\ X^s_{i,n}=x\}.
\]
The row-\(n\) empirical source outcome-moment vector \(\widehat z_{x,y,n}\) is defined by
\[
\widehat z_{x,y,n}(e)
=
\frac{1}{n_s(n)}
\sum_{i=1}^{n_s(n)}
\mathbf 1\{E^s_{i,n}=e,\ X^s_{i,n}=x,\ Y^s_{i,n}=y\}.
\]
The row-\(n\) empirical target proxy vector \(\widehat b_n\) is defined by
\[
\widehat b_n(w)
=
\frac{1}{n_t(n)}
\sum_{j=1}^{n_t(n)}
\mathbf 1\{W^t_{j,n}=w\}.
\]
Define the truncated-SVD Wald estimator by
\[
\widehat\theta^{\,W}_{x,y,n}
=
\phi_{r_0}(\widehat H_{x,n},\widehat z_{x,y,n},\widehat b_n).
\]

\\operatorname{Fin}(•).title: Canonical finite index sets
\\operatorname{Fin}(•).body: For an integer \(n\ge1\), \(\operatorname{Fin}(n)\) denotes the finite index set \(\{0,1,\ldots,n-1\}\). In particular, \(\operatorname{Fin}(2)=\{0,1\}\) and \(\operatorname{Fin}(3)=\{0,1,2\}\), used as finite state spaces with cardinalities \(|\operatorname{Fin}(2)|=2\) and \(|\operatorname{Fin}(3)|=3\).

\\Gamma_{x,y}(•).title: Joint multinomial covariance
\\Gamma_{x,y}(•).body: Fix \(p\in(0,1)\) and \(\mathcal M\in\mathfrak M_{+}\). Let \(T_{x,y}=(\operatorname{vec}H_x,z_{x,y},b)\), and let \(\widehat T_{x,y,n}=(\operatorname{vec}\widehat H_{x,n},\widehat z_{x,y,n},\widehat b_n)\) be formed from independent source and target samples with \(n_s(n)/n\to p\) and \(n_t(n)/n\to1-p\). Define \(\Gamma_{x,y}(\mathcal M;p)\) to be the covariance matrix of the centered Gaussian limit of \(\sqrt n(\widehat T_{x,y,n}-T_{x,y})\). Equivalently, its source block is \(p^{-1}\) times the multinomial covariance of the source cell indicators defining \(H_x\) and \(z_{x,y}\) under \(P_O\), its target block is \((1-p)^{-1}\) times the multinomial covariance of the target proxy indicators defining \(b\), and the source--target cross blocks are zero.

\\mathcal\u0001E.title: Finite latent-shift state spaces
\\mathcal\u0001E.body: The latent-shift state spaces are finite sets \(\mathcal E,\mathcal U,\mathcal W,\mathcal X,\mathcal Y\), where \(\mathcal E\) is the source-environment state space and \(\mathcal X\) is the treatment state space, both nonempty. The latent state space \(\mathcal U\) has cardinality \(r=\lvert\mathcal U\rvert\) with \(2\le r\). The proxy state space \(\mathcal W\) has cardinality \(m=\lvert\mathcal W\rvert\) with \(m\ge r\). The outcome state space \(\mathcal Y\) satisfies \(\lvert\mathcal Y\rvert\ge2\).

normalizedfinitelatent-shiftSCM.title: Normalized finite latent-shift SCM
normalizedfinitelatent-shiftSCM.body: A normalized finite latent-shift SCM on finite state spaces \(\mathcal E,\mathcal U,\mathcal W,\mathcal X,\mathcal Y\) is a tuple \(\mathcal M=(\pi,S,M,a,f,q)\) Markov relative to the graph with arrows \(E\to U\), \(U\to W\), \(U\to X\), \(U\to Y\), \(W\to Y\), and \(X\to Y\). The primitive \(\pi\in\Delta^{\circ}(\mathcal E)\) is a strictly positive environment law; \(S\in\mathbb R^{r\times\lvert\mathcal E\rvert}\) is a strictly positive column-stochastic latent channel with \(S_{ue}=P(U=u\mid E=e)\); \(M\in\mathbb R^{m\times r}\) is a strictly positive column-stochastic proxy channel with \(M_{wu}=P(W=w\mid U=u)\); \(a\) is a strictly positive treatment kernel with \(a_x(u)=P(X=x\mid U=u)\); \(f\) is a strictly positive outcome kernel with \(f_{x,y}(u,w)=P(Y=y\mid U=u,W=w,X=x)\); and \(q\in\Delta^{\circ}(\mathcal U)\) is a strictly positive target latent mixture with \(q_u=Q(U=u)\). Normalization means \(\sum_e\pi_e=1\), \(\sum_u S_{ue}=1\) for each \(e\), \(\sum_w M_{wu}=1\) for each \(u\), \(\sum_x a_x(u)=1\) for each \(u\), \(\sum_y f_{x,y}(u,w)=1\) for each \((u,w,x)\), and \(\sum_u q_u=1\). The SCM induces the source full-data law \(P_{\mathcal M}\) on \(\mathcal E\times\mathcal U\times\mathcal W\times\mathcal X\times\mathcal Y\) with cell probabilities \(P_{\mathcal M}(e,u,w,x,y)=\pi_e S_{ue}M_{wu}a_x(u)f_{x,y}(u,w)\), and the target law \(Q_{\mathcal M}\) on \(\mathcal U\times\mathcal W\times\mathcal X\times\mathcal Y\) with cell probabilities \(Q_{\mathcal M}(u,w,x,y)=q_uM_{wu}a_x(u)f_{x,y}(u,w)\).
